# AIVAX Documentation

> Build, operate, and evaluate AI applications with AIVAX.

Language: English. Embedded API references are linked, not fetched.

# AIVAX Documentation

AIVAX is an AI orchestration platform for building, operating, and evaluating AI applications through one account and API surface. Use hosted or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) models, then add reusable instructions, knowledge, tools, media, user channels, and background processing as your product grows.

## Choose where to start

- **Make your first model call:** follow [Make your first request](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.md#make-your-first-request) for a minimal OpenAI-compatible chat completion.
- **Understand the platform:** read the [Welcome](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.md) page to choose between direct inference, AI Gateways, RAG, generations, Batch, and other products.
- **Prepare a production integration:** review [Authentication](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/authentication.md), [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md), and [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md).

## Build an AI application

- [Inference](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md) — generate responses with hosted or BYOK models through an OpenAI-compatible API.
- [AI Gateways](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md) — reuse a model, instructions, RAG, skills, tools, moderation, and inference settings as one assistant runtime.
- [RAG collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md) — index your own knowledge for semantic search and grounded answers.
- [Rerankers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md) — reorder candidate documents by relevance, with or without a managed collection.
- [Skills](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/skills.md) — package reusable instructions and operating knowledge for AI Gateways.
- [Tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md) and [MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/mcp.md) — connect assistants to AIVAX capabilities and external systems.
- [Chat clients](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md) — publish a gateway through web chat or supported messaging integrations.

## Process text and media

- [Text classification](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/classification.md) and [text segmentation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/text-segmentation.md) — prepare documents for routing, analysis, and retrieval.
- [Image generation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/images.md) — create or edit images from text and reference images.
- [Speech generation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/speech.md) and [audio transcription](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/audio-transcriptions.md) — convert between text and audio.
- [Media descriptions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/media-descriptions.md) — turn images, audio, video, or files into text for downstream processing.
- [Voice Sessions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/voice-session.md) — build low-latency, two-way voice experiences.

## Operate at scale and improve quality

- [Batch](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/batch.md) — run the same AI workflow over many independent items in the background.
- [Agentic Tests](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/agentic-tests.md) — evaluate complete, goal-oriented conversations and track repeatable gateway regressions.
- [Structured responses](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/structured-responses/concepts.md) — validate generated JSON against an application contract.
- [MCP utilities](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/account-management-mcp.md) — expose account, collection, documentation, web, and inference capabilities to compatible agents.

For endpoint schemas and generated request details, use the [AIVAX API reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.html

# Welcome

AIVAX is an AI orchestration platform for building, operating, and evaluating AI applications. It gives you one account, one API surface, and one billing wallet.

It combines:

- Hosted and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) models.
- Reusable assistant configuration.
- Knowledge retrieval and tools.
- Text and media processing.
- User-facing channels.
- Background jobs.
- Conversational evaluation.

You do not need every product for every application. Start with direct inference when you only need a response. Add other products when you need to:

- Reuse assistant settings.
- Search your documents.
- Connect tools or channels.
- Process many records.
- Evaluate behavior.

## Choose the right starting point

Use this table when you know the job and need the first product to open. Each row is a starting point, not a complete architecture.

| Goal | Start with | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generate or analyze text in one request | [Inference](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md) | Call a hosted or BYOK model through the OpenAI-compatible API without creating reusable assistant configuration. |
| Reuse instructions, knowledge, tools, and model settings | [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md) | Give your application one stable assistant runtime that can evolve without rebuilding every request. |
| Search your own documents or generate grounded answers | [RAG collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md) | Store and index knowledge for semantic retrieval, citations, and gateway context. |
| Reorder candidates your application already retrieved | [Rerankers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md) | Improve relevance without requiring a managed AIVAX collection. |
| Publish an assistant to end users | [Chat clients](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md) | Connect a gateway to web chat or supported messaging integrations with session and channel controls. |
| Process many independent records | [Batch](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/batch.md) | Run one repeatable workflow asynchronously with per-item state, validation, retries, cost, and export. |
| Test a complete assistant conversation | [Agentic Tests](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/agentic-tests.md) | Simulate a goal-oriented user and judge the gateway across multiple turns. |
| Build a low-latency two-way voice experience | [Voice Sessions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/voice-session.md) | Stream user and assistant audio in an interactive session instead of combining separate audio jobs. |

## Build the assistant runtime

This is the core path for an assistant that answers users. Start here when the application needs a model call, reusable settings, knowledge, or tools.

### Inference and AI Gateways

AIVAX exposes OpenAI-compatible model listing and chat completion endpoints. Use this layer when the application needs a generated response.

- Use a **direct model call** for exploration, one-off generation, or configuration that does not need to be reused.
- Use an **AI Gateway** when the same model, instructions, RAG collections, skills, tools, moderation, or output behavior should serve multiple calls or users.

Most production assistants use a gateway. The application can keep calling one identifier while the assistant configuration changes independently. Gateways can use integrated AIVAX models or external OpenAI-compatible providers.

Production API base URL:

```text
https://inference.aivax.net
```

OpenAI-compatible SDK base URL:

```text
https://inference.aivax.net/v1
```

Reference:

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Inference%20(chat%20completions))

### Knowledge, retrieval, and reranking

A [RAG collection](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md) is a semantic knowledge library. Use it when answers should come from your own documents.

1. Add documents.
2. Test them with [Semantic Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md).
3. Attach the collection to an AI Gateway when the assistant should answer from that knowledge.

AIVAX can also generate grounded answers directly from collections and expose collection search through [Collections MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/collections-mcp.md).

Reranking is a separate step. It receives a query and candidate documents, then returns the candidates in a more relevant order.

- Use a collection for managed storage and retrieval.
- Use the standalone [reranking](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md) generation when your application already owns the candidates.

### Skills and tools

[Skills](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/skills.md) package reusable instructions and operating knowledge. Use them when the same procedure should apply across requests.

- Use a skill when the assistant needs to know **how** to perform a task.
- Use RAG when it needs to retrieve **facts or source material** that may grow or change independently.
- Use a tool when the assistant must take action or retrieve live information.

Choose among:

- [Built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md) for capabilities provided by AIVAX.
- [MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/mcp.md) for Model Context Protocol servers and reusable tool ecosystems.
- [Protocol functions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/protocol-functions.md) for HTTP functions defined by your application.
- [Shell](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/shell.md) for controlled command execution when the use case requires it.

Keep the tool surface as small as the assistant's job allows. Each additional tool expands cost, latency, permissions, and failure paths.

## Process text, documents, and media

Use these products when the job is a focused transformation and does not need a full chat conversation:

- [Text classification](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/classification.md) assigns labels to one or more documents.
- [Text segmentation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/text-segmentation.md) splits long content into useful chunks for indexing or downstream processing.
- [Media descriptions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/media-descriptions.md) convert images, audio, video, and files into text that another model or workflow can use.
- [Image generation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/images.md) creates or edits images.
- [Speech generation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/speech.md) turns text into audio.
- [Audio transcription](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/audio-transcriptions.md) turns audio into text.

Choose the path by what you need back:

- Use direct multimodal inference when the selected chat model supports the input and should reason over it in the same request.
- Use a focused generation endpoint when you need a reusable artifact, a transcript, a description, or a preprocessing stage.
- For large independent input sets, run the appropriate operation through [Batch](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/batch.md).

For interactive two-way audio, use [Voice Sessions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/voice-session.md) instead of manually chaining transcription, text inference, and speech generation.

## Deliver, scale, and evaluate

Use these products after the assistant runtime works. They publish it to users, run it across many records, or check whether it behaves as intended.

### Chat clients

A [chat client](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md) connects an AI Gateway to an end-user channel. Use it for a browser widget or a supported messaging integration. Use the inference API directly when your own backend or interface already manages users, conversation state, and delivery.

A chat client owns presentation, session behavior, allowed origins, uploads, audio replies, channel integrations, and user-facing limits. The gateway continues to own assistant behavior such as the model, instructions, RAG, and tools.

### Batch

[Batch](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/batch.md) applies one workflow to dozens or thousands of independent records. Use it when each record is independent and the caller does not need an immediate answer.

A workflow defines the instruction, model or gateway, structured output, validation, tools, and retry policy. A job then:

1. Imports items.
2. Processes them in the background.
3. Exposes per-item progress and cost.
4. Exports results.

Do not use Batch when one item depends on another or when a user needs an immediate answer. Use direct inference for one synchronous result and RAG for searchable knowledge.

### Agentic Tests

[Agentic Tests](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/agentic-tests.md) evaluate the configured behavior of an AI Gateway across a bounded conversation. A simulated user pursues a goal while an independent judge evaluates progress.

- Use persisted tests for reusable, scheduled regression coverage.
- Use an ephemeral evaluation for one immediate run.

A completed test run is not automatically a successful behavior result. Review these together:

- Run outcome.
- Judge result.
- Retained conversation.
- Usage.
- Cost.

## Operate and connect AIVAX

Use this section to trace cost, connect a compatible agent, or operate the account from scripts.

AIVAX records conversations and usage so you can trace behavior, attribute cost, and diagnose failures. The dashboard and account APIs expose:

- Account balance.
- Usage.
- Conversations.
- Gateway resources.
- Collection transactions.
- Batch items.
- Agentic Test runs.

Start with [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md) and [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md) before enabling a high-volume or media-heavy workflow.

AIVAX also provides MCP utilities for compatible agents:

- [Account management MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/account-management-mcp.md)
- [Collections MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/collections-mcp.md)
- [Documentation MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/documentation-mcp.md)
- [Web utilities MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/web-utilities-mcp.md)
- [Media generation MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/media-generation-mcp.md)
- [Inference MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/inference-mcp.md)

These utilities expose existing AIVAX capabilities through MCP. They do not replace the underlying account, collection, or inference products.

To operate an account from the terminal or from scripts, install the [AIVAX CLI](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/cli.md) with `npm install -g @aivax/cli`.

## Make your first request

Use this path for the first successful chat completion. It calls a hosted model or an AI Gateway through the OpenAI-compatible API.

1. Create a **private** key in the API Keys area of the AIVAX dashboard.
2. Store it as a secret, for example in an environment variable named `AIVAX_API_KEY`.
3. Install the OpenAI SDK with `python -m pip install openai`.
4. Create `quickstart.py`:

```python
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.aivax.net/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["AIVAX_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="<MODEL_OR_GATEWAY_ID>",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Write a one-sentence welcome message."}
    ],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

Replace `<MODEL_OR_GATEWAY_ID>` with a hosted model name from the model listing or with an AI Gateway identifier. Then run `python quickstart.py`.

A successful request prints one generated sentence. If it fails, see [Troubleshoot requests](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/troubleshooting.md).

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Model%20listing)

## Long-running inference

Use the direct inference host when a request ends with HTTP `524` or a proxy timeout while AIVAX is still processing it:

```text
https://direct.inference.aivax.net/v1
```

The request remains synchronous, not a background job.

1. Keep the client connection open until the completion finishes.
2. Configure a client timeout that covers the expected processing time.
3. Use the same private API key, model or AI Gateway identifier, messages, and request parameters.
4. Change the SDK base URL and timeout:

```python
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://direct.inference.aivax.net/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["AIVAX_API_KEY"],
    timeout=300.0,
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="<MODEL_OR_GATEWAY_ID>",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Analyze this case carefully and provide a detailed recommendation.",
        }
    ],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

### Endpoints available on the direct host

Use this list to confirm that the direct host serves the call you need. It serves only the endpoints below. Paths, authentication, request bodies, and responses are the same as on `https://inference.aivax.net`; only the host changes.

| Method | Path | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` or `/api/v1/chat/completions` | [Chat completions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md) with an integrated model or an AI Gateway |
| `GET` | `/v1/models` or `/api/v1/models` | [Model listing](#make-your-first-request) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/public/chat-clients/<access-key>/prompt` | [Send a prompt to a chat-client session](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md#sending-prompts-from-your-application) |
| `POST` | `/api/v2/query`, `/api/v2/query/similar`, or `/api/v2/query/browse` | [Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/answer` | [RAG answer generation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md#where-filters-are-supported) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/images` | [Image generation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/images.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/speech` | [Speech synthesis](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/speech.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/audio/transcriptions` | [Audio transcription](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/audio-transcriptions.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/descriptions` | [Media descriptions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/media-descriptions.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/classify` | [Classification](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/classification.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/segment` | [Text segmentation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/text-segmentation.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/decisions` | [Decisions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/decisions.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/rerank` | [Reranking](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/agentic-tests` | [Ephemeral agentic test evaluation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/agentic-tests.md) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/generations/teach-skill` | Teach skill from a tutorial video |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/web/fetch` | [Web fetch and OCR](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/web-foundation/fetch-and-ocr.md) |

Compatibility aliases of these generation endpoints, such as `/api/v1/generations/validations` and `/api/v1/generations/reflex/rerank`, are also served.

Any other path returns `404 Not Found` on the direct host. Account management, AI Gateway, collection, document, batch, and other administrative APIs, including web search, remain available only on `https://inference.aivax.net`.

The endpoints most likely to need the direct host are:

- Non-streaming chat completions with long reasoning or many tool calls.
- Image generation on slower models.
- Media descriptions and transcriptions of large files.
- Teach skill.
- Chat-client prompts that run long tool chains.

Streaming chat completions send data continuously and rarely need it.

## Next steps

After the first request succeeds, continue in this order:

1. Make your first request with the example above, then read [Inference](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md) for the full request contract.
2. Read [Authentication](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/authentication.md) before choosing private keys, public keys, or chat sessions for an application boundary.
3. Review [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md) and [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md) before increasing traffic or processing large collections, media, tests, or Batch jobs.
4. Move reusable assistant behavior into an [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md), then add RAG, skills, tools, and a chat client only when the use case requires them.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/authentication.html

# Authentication

AIVAX authenticates API requests with account API keys. A login key is a separate credential and only opens the console.

AIVAX accepts API keys via:

- `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`
- `Authorization: Basic <BASE64_USERNAME_COLON_API_KEY>`
- `?api-key=<API_KEY>`

Choose how to send the key:

- Prefer `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` for server-to-server calls.
- `Authorization: Basic <BASE64_USERNAME_COLON_API_KEY>` is also accepted.
- Use `?api-key=<API_KEY>` only when a client or integration cannot send headers, because URLs can be logged by proxies, browsers, and monitoring tools.

## API key types

A key type decides which routes the caller can use. Choose it from where the code runs and who owns the account.

AIVAX has two key families because browser-facing and server-side use cases have different risk profiles. If your code runs on your server, use a private key and keep it out of client bundles, logs, and public repositories. If your code runs in a browser or another environment where the key can be inspected by the end user, use a public key and keep the workflow limited to routes designed for public access. Application keys are a third type: an account holder approves them for a third-party application through [OAuth](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/oauth.md).

| Type | Prefix | Intended use | Access |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Private key | `sk-aiv-acc` | Server-side integrations and administrative API calls. | Every authenticated account API except API key and credential management. |
| Public key | `pk-aiv-` | Restricted client-side calls. | Text inference, generations, and RAG retrieval. |
| Application key | `sk-aiv-apk` | Third-party applications authorized by the account holder. | The permissions approved through [OAuth](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/oauth.md), plus the account identity. |

Each key type grants a fixed set of permissions, and each route requires some of them. A request whose key lacks a permission required by the route returns `403 Forbidden`, and the error message names the missing permissions.

### Private keys

Use a private key for backend services, account management, model listing, collection management, batch operations, and any workflow that needs the full gateway tool surface.

Private keys cannot list, create, or delete API keys, roll the account salt, manage authenticators, or reset the login key. Use the dashboard for these operations.

For a first server-side request, continue with [Make your first request](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.md#make-your-first-request).

### Public keys

Use a public key only for routes designed for public access. A public key can call:

- chat completions;
- the `/api/v1/generations/*` endpoints;
- RAG semantic search;
- RAG answer generation.

A public key cannot:

- read or change account resources;
- open voice sessions;
- use the web search and fetch endpoints.

When a public key calls chat completions:

- The `model` must be a full AI Gateway UUID; direct integrated-model calls and gateway slug lookup are disabled.
- MCP sources, protocol functions, built-in tools, Bash, skills, and sentinel options are stripped from the request.
- Only these request parameters are accepted: `model`, `messages`, `prompt`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `seed`, `tools`, `reasoning_effort`, `max_completion_tokens`, `conversation_token`, `idempotency_key`, and `stream`.
- Request and token rate limits are applied both globally per key and per remote address. See [Public API keys](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#public-api-keys) for the current values.

If you are exposing a browser or widget experience to end users, review [Chat Clients](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md) before deciding whether a public key is the right boundary.

### Application keys

Use an application key when a third-party application should call AIVAX with the account holder's permission. The key receives the permissions approved through [OAuth](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/oauth.md), plus the account identity. See [OAuth authorization](#oauth-authorization) for the short version, and [OAuth](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/oauth.md) for the complete flow.

## Manage keys

Create and revoke API keys in the API Keys area of the AIVAX dashboard. Use this area when you need a new key, a label, an expiration date, or a revocation.

Keys belong to an account and can have a label, expiration, and type. Expired keys are rejected by authentication.

Create separate keys for separate applications. That makes rotation safer: if one integration is compromised, you can revoke only that key instead of breaking every service tied to the account. Use labels to identify each key's owner and application, and expiration dates to plan when to renew or replace it.

## OAuth authorization

OAuth lets a third-party application ask an AIVAX account holder for an application key instead of asking them to copy an API key. Use it when the person who owns the account is not the developer of the application.

The account holder reviews the request in the console, chooses how long the access lasts, and can revoke it at any time. See [OAuth](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/oauth.md) for the complete flow, permissions and callback handling.

## Send a key with Bearer auth

Use this pattern when an OpenAI-compatible SDK should call AIVAX. Pass the AIVAX key as the SDK API key and set the base URL to `https://inference.aivax.net/v1`.

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.aivax.net/v1",
    api_key="<AIVAX_API_KEY>"
)
```

## Hook authentication

Hook authentication lets your service verify outbound AIVAX requests. Use it for AI Gateway workers and server-side protocol functions.

This is the reverse direction of normal API authentication:

1. In a normal API call, your application proves it is allowed to call AIVAX by sending an API key.
2. In a worker or protocol-function callback, AIVAX calls your service.
3. Your service needs a way to verify that the request really came from the account configuration you control.

That is what `X-Request-Nonce` is for.

If your account has a hook key, AIVAX sends:

```text
X-Request-Nonce: <BCrypt hash>
```

The nonce is a BCrypt hash derived from the account hook key. Validate the header by verifying the stored plain-text hook key against the hash. If the account has no hook key, the header is not sent.

Rolling the hook key invalidates existing worker and integration validation secrets.

### C# example

```csharp
using BCrypt.Net;

var nonce = request.Headers["X-Request-Nonce"];
var hookKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AIVAX_HOOK_SECRET");

if (nonce is null || hookKey is null)
{
    return Results.Unauthorized();
}

if (!BCrypt.Net.BCrypt.Verify(hookKey, nonce, enhancedEntropy: false))
{
    return Results.Forbid();
}
```

### Python example

```python
import os
import bcrypt
from flask import abort, request

nonce = request.headers.get("X-Request-Nonce")
hook_key = os.getenv("AIVAX_HOOK_SECRET")

if nonce is None or hook_key is None:
    abort(401)

if not bcrypt.checkpw(hook_key.encode("utf-8"), nonce.encode("utf-8")):
    abort(403)
```

### JavaScript example

```javascript
import bcrypt from "bcrypt";

const nonce = req.header("X-Request-Nonce");
const hookKey = process.env.AIVAX_HOOK_SECRET;

if (!nonce || !hookKey) {
  return res.sendStatus(401);
}

if (!(await bcrypt.compare(hookKey, nonce))) {
  return res.sendStatus(403);
}
```

## Console sign-in

The console at `console.aivax.net` signs in with the login key e-mailed when the account is created. Use this section when you need to open the console, add an authenticator, or recover a login key.

A login key is not an API key. It only opens a console session. API keys continue to call the API without a login key or authenticator code.

### Two-factor authentication

Account holders can add one or more authenticator apps from **My account**, **Security**. Use an authenticator when console sign-in should require a current code as well as the login key.

1. Add one or more authenticator apps from **My account**, **Security**.
2. Confirm the six-digit code from that app. The QR code and secret are shown only while that code is confirmed.
3. After confirmation, the secret cannot be viewed again.

When at least one authenticator is confirmed:

- Console sign-in asks for a current six-digit code.
- Switching to that saved account asks for a current six-digit code.
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` accepts an optional `totpCode`.
- If the login key is valid and the code is missing, the response has `requiresTwoFactor: true` and does not create a session.
- Send the same login key again with `totpCode`.

Accounts without an authenticator are unchanged.

Removing the last authenticator disables the prompt. Disabling two-factor authentication without a current code is handled by [AIVAX support](https://aivax.net/contact/).

### Recover access

The sign-in page links to account support. Use these paths when the account holder cannot sign in.

#### Recover login key

**Recover login key** asks for the registration e-mail. AIVAX shows the same confirmation whether or not that e-mail belongs to an account.

When the e-mail belongs to an account, the message contains:

- a one-time sign-in link;
- a link to reset the login key.

Both links expire in one hour.

- The sign-in link still asks for an authenticator code when two-factor authentication is enabled.
- The reset link creates a new login key, e-mails it, and signs the account out of every console session.
- The reset link does not disable two-factor authentication or revoke API keys.

#### Disable two-factor authentication

**Disable two-factor authentication** opens [AIVAX support](https://aivax.net/contact/).

#### Registration e-mail no longer available

If the registration e-mail is no longer available, use the same [support page](https://aivax.net/contact/).

#### Reset the login key in Security

Resetting the login key from **Security** asks for confirmation, then does the same rotation:

- A new key is e-mailed.
- Console sessions are signed out.
- The browser's saved login is cleared.

API keys keep working.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/oauth.html

# OAuth

OAuth lets your application use a person's AIVAX account for its AI features. Instead of building your own model access, billing and limits, your application asks the account holder for permission, and AIVAX gives it an access token limited to what the person approved.

It is designed for applications that need AI resources but should not own them: desktop and mobile apps, editor plugins, browser extensions, automation tools and SaaS products where each user brings their own AIVAX account. The account holder keeps control of the account. Requests made with the token use that account's models, AI gateways, collections and balance, and the person can revoke the access at any time.

## When to use it

Use OAuth when the person who owns the AIVAX account is not the developer of the application. They should never have to copy an API key into a third-party product, and the application should only receive the permissions it needs.

Use OAuth when:

- the account holder is not the developer of the application;
- the person should not copy an API key into your product;
- the application needs only the permissions it will use.

Use a [private or public API key](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/authentication.md#api-key-types) when the application and the AIVAX account belong to you. For example, a backend that serves your own users with your own AIVAX account should use a private key.

## How it works

Authorization is a browser handoff. Your application creates a request, the person reviews it in the console, and AIVAX returns the result to your callback.

1. Your application creates an authorization request with its name, the reason it needs access, the permissions it wants and the address that receives the result.
2. Your application sends the person to the authorization address returned by AIVAX.
3. The person signs in to the AIVAX console if needed, reviews the request and chooses how long the access lasts: 1 day, 7 days, 90 days or 1 year.
4. AIVAX redirects the person back to your application with an access token, or with an error if access was denied.
5. Your application calls the AIVAX API with the token, like any other API key.

No refresh token is issued. When the token expires or is revoked, start a new authorization.

## Create an authorization request

Use this call when your application is ready to send a person to the AIVAX console. This endpoint does not require authentication and is rate limited per remote address.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Create%20OAuth%20Authorization%20Request)

### Request body

The request body has:

- `clientName`: the name shown to the person, from 3 to 64 characters.
- `reason`: why your application needs access, from 3 to 500 characters and at most 6 lines. Be specific, for example "Summarize your meeting notes with your AI gateways".
- `permissions`: the [permissions](#permissions) your application needs.
- `returnUrl`: the address that receives the result.

### Return URL

The `returnUrl` must:

- be an absolute `http` or `https` address;
- contain no credentials;
- contain no fragment;
- not point to the AIVAX console;
- not repeat query parameters;
- not already contain `access_token`, `expires_in` or `error` in its query.

### Response

The response has:

- `authorizationUrl`: the console address where the person approves the request.
- `expiresIn`: seconds until the request expires.

The request expires after one hour and can be approved or denied once.

## Send the person to the console

Open the returned address in the person's browser. Do this before the request expires.

1. Open `authorizationUrl` in the person's browser.
2. The console asks them to sign in when they are not signed in, and returns to the request afterwards.
3. The console shows your application name, the reason, the requested permissions and the full return address.
4. The **Authorize** button stays disabled for five seconds so the request can be read.
5. Authorizing requires a browser check.

## Receive the token

Your `returnUrl` receives the decision as query parameters. Handle that callback on your server, then store the token as a secret.

### Query parameters

After approval, AIVAX redirects the person to `returnUrl` with these query parameters:

- `access_token`: the application key, starting with `sk-aiv-apk`.
- `expires_in`: the token lifetime, in seconds.

If the person denies access, the query has `error=access_denied` instead.

Query parameters already present in `returnUrl` are kept.

### Check state

Add your own random `state` value when you create the request. This check confirms that the callback belongs to a request your application started.

1. Store `state` in the person's session.
2. Compare it in the callback.
3. Accept the result only when the values match.

### Store the token on the server

The token arrives in a URL. Treat the callback as sensitive:

1. Read the token on your server.
2. Store it as a secret.
3. Redirect the browser to an address without it.
4. Do not log callback URLs or send the token to the browser.

```javascript
app.get("/oauth/callback", async (req, res) => {
  if (!req.query.state || req.query.state !== req.session.oauthState) {
    return res.status(400).send("Invalid state.");
  }

  if (req.query.error) {
    return res.redirect("/settings?aivax=denied");
  }

  if (!req.query.access_token) {
    return res.status(400).send("Missing token.");
  }

  await saveAivaxToken(req.session.userId, {
    token: req.query.access_token,
    expiresAt: Date.now() + Number(req.query.expires_in) * 1000
  });

  res.redirect("/settings?aivax=connected");
});
```

## Use the token

Send the token like any other API key, preferably in the `Authorization` header. For OpenAI-compatible SDKs, pass it as the API key and set the base URL to `https://inference.aivax.net/v1`.

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.aivax.net/v1",
    api_key="<ACCESS_TOKEN>"
)
```

Usage made with the token is charged to the account that authorized your application. Every application key can call `GET /api/v1/accounts` to read the account identifier, name and e-mail, so your application can show which account it is connected to.

A request that needs a permission the token does not have returns `403 Forbidden`, and the error message names the missing permissions. A revoked or expired token returns `401 Unauthorized`; ask the person to connect again.

## Permissions

Request only what your application uses. The console shows each permission to the person before they approve it.

- `InferenceText`: chat completions with models and AI gateways.
- `InferenceGenerations`: image, speech, transcription, decision, extraction and other generations.
- `InferenceRealtime`: realtime voice sessions.
- `ResourcesRead`: read AI gateways, chat clients, batch, skills, shell sandbox files and other resources, and list models.
- `ResourcesWrite`: create, edit and delete those resources.
- `RagRead`: semantic search and reading documents of RAG collections.
- `RagWrite`: create, edit and delete RAG collections and documents.
- `ManagementAnalytics`: read balance, consumption and billing information.
- `Account`: payments, subscriptions, plan changes, notifications and other account-level operations.
- `WebUtilities`: web search and URL fetching.

`ManagementKeys` cannot be requested, so application keys can never list, create or delete API keys or manage the account credentials.

## Revoke access

The account holder revokes an application from the console. Use this section to tell them where to review or remove access.

In **My account**, **Authorized applications**, the account holder can see:

- every authorized application;
- its permissions;
- its expiration;
- its last use.

Revoking an application invalidates the token immediately.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/cli.html

# CLI tool

The AIVAX CLI operates an AIVAX account from the terminal. It covers the same products as the API, including AI Gateways, RAG collections, chat clients, Batch, Agentic Tests, web search, OCR, generations, conversations, skills, logs, and account settings, without requiring you to write HTTP requests.

The CLI is open source under the MIT license and published on npm as [`@aivax/cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aivax/cli).

## When to use it

Use the CLI when a person or an agent works with an account interactively or from scripts:

- inspecting and adjusting gateways, collections, and chat clients without opening the dashboard;
- importing documents into a collection, or transcribing a long PDF page by page into Markdown or RAG-ready JSONL;
- creating, starting, and exporting Batch jobs from local files;
- running Agentic Tests, checking consumption, or reading conversations and logs while debugging;
- giving a coding agent a compact way to operate AIVAX, since responses are optimized for agents by default.

For application code that serves end users, call the [API](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.md#make-your-first-request) or an OpenAI-compatible SDK directly instead.

## Install

The CLI requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.19 or newer.

```bash
npm install -g @aivax/cli
aivax auth login
```

Other package managers also work, such as `pnpm add -g @aivax/cli` or `bun install -g @aivax/cli`.

`aivax auth login` saves an account profile. The access key is kept in the operating system credential store. To link a profile without sharing the account login key, for example when a coding agent sets up the CLI, pass an existing API key instead:

```bash
aivax auth login --api-key <API_KEY> --profile-name <PROFILE_NAME>
```

For scripts and CI, set the `AIVAX_API_KEY` environment variable instead of logging in.

## What it can do

Ask a gateway about a local file:

```bash
aivax gateways chat -m <GATEWAY_ID> "Summarize this contract" -f contract.pdf --stream
```

Search a collection, or transcribe a document and index it:

```bash
aivax rag search --collection <COLLECTION_ID> -q "refund policy" -k 10
aivax ocr document manual.pdf --format jsonl -o manual.jsonl
aivax rag import -c <COLLECTION_ID> -f manual.jsonl
```

Run a Batch job from a JSONL file and export the results:

```bash
aivax batch items import -w <WORKFLOW_ID> -j <JOB_ID> -f customers.jsonl
aivax batch jobs start -w <WORKFLOW_ID> -j <JOB_ID>
aivax batch jobs export -w <WORKFLOW_ID> -j <JOB_ID> -o results.jsonl
```

Generate media, search the web, or check spending:

```bash
aivax generate speech -m <MODEL_ID> -t @script.txt -o narration.mp3
aivax web search -q "AI regulation news" --country US
aivax analytics balance
```

Call any endpoint that has no dedicated command:

```bash
aivax api get /api/v1/notifications/unread/count
```

Run `aivax --help` to list every command group, and add `--help` to any command to see its options. `aivax docs reference <ENDPOINT_NAME>` shows the API reference for an endpoint without leaving the terminal.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.html

# Pricing

AIVAX charges usage to the account balance in USD. Each product documents its own rates in a dedicated pricing section, linked below. This page covers the rules shared by every product: subscription allowances, storage, the request cost header, the data sharing discount, plan multipliers, and credit top-up fees.

See [subscription pricing](https://aivax.net/pricing) for monthly plan prices and [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md) for account-level quotas. **M** means one million tokens; **1k** means one thousand units. Approximate prices (`~`) vary with the model used and the work performed.

## Plan list prices

Use the pricing page when you are choosing a plan in a browser. To read the same public list prices from an application, call `GET /api/v1/information/plans.json`. No API key is required. The response lists Free, Pro, Max, and Ultimate. Each entry has `plan` and `monthlyPrice` in USD. Free is `0` because that plan has no subscription fee. A negotiated Custom price, or the price currently applied to an account, is not included. Use the Subscriptions API when you need the authenticated account's price.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Get%20Plans)

## Product pricing

| Area | Where to find rates |
| --- | --- |
| Inference and moderation | [Inference](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md#pricing) |
| Agentic Tests | [Agentic Tests](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/agentic-tests.md#pricing-and-limits) |
| Voice and Realtime | [Voice and Realtime](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/voice-session.md#billing-and-limits) |
| RAG collections, search, and answers | [Collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md#pricing-and-limits) |
| Media Injector | [Documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md#pricing-and-limits) |
| Reflex | [Reflex](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reflex.md#pricing-and-limits) |
| Web search and X search | [Web Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/web-foundation/web-search.md) |
| Fetch and OCR | [Fetch and OCR](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/web-foundation/fetch-and-ocr.md) |
| Image generation | [Image generation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/images.md) |
| Text-to-speech and speech-to-text | [Text-to-speech](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/speech.md) and [Speech-to-text](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/audio-transcriptions.md) |
| Media descriptions, decisions, classification, and segmentation | [Data processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/media-descriptions.md) pages |
| Document extraction and summarization | [Extraction](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/extraction.md) and [Summarization](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/summarization.md) |
| Translations | [Translations](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/translations.md) |
| Built-in tools and memory | [Built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md) |

## Included daily allowances

Every plan includes separate daily allowances for eligible RAG embeddings, Reflex reranking, eligible semantic decisions, and Fetch/OCR extraction. Product rates apply when a metered item is not covered. Coverage is all-or-nothing per item, not necessarily per complete request: an item that cannot fit within the remaining allowance and its permitted margin is billed in full. Compare the allowances and check exclusions in [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#included-daily-subscription-allowances). LLM subscription coverage is currently disabled. For what each allowance covers, see [Free RAG API on AIVAX Free](https://aivax.net/blog/free-tier-for-rag-reflex-decisions-and-ocr/).

## Storage

Each plan includes storage. Pro, Max, and Ultimate overages are billed hourly at the monthly rates below; Free storage cannot be expanded. Document text stored in a collection counts as UTF-8 bytes. Text with accents or non-Latin characters can use more of the included quota than basic Latin text of the same length.

| Description | Pricing |
| --- | ---: |
| Free storage | **30 MB included**; no expansion |
| Pro storage | **2 GB included**; excess **$0.50/GB/month** |
| Max storage | **10 GB included**; excess **$0.30/GB/month** |
| Ultimate storage | **20 GB included**; excess **$0.20/GB/month** |

## Request cost header

API responses include a `Consumed-Credits` header when the request charged usage to your account balance. Its value is the total charged by that request in USD, written as a decimal number with a dot separator, for example `Consumed-Credits: 0.000184`. It already includes the plan multiplier and covers every item charged during the request, such as inference, embeddings, reranking, and tool usage.

Cross-origin responses expose `Consumed-Credits` and `X-Request-ID`, so browser JavaScript on another origin can read them when they are present. `X-Request-ID` is the identifier AIVAX assigned to that request.

The header is omitted when the request charged nothing, including requests rejected by validation or covered entirely by a daily subscription allowance. Treat a missing header as zero.

The value only covers charges recorded before the response is sent. Usage recorded later, such as asynchronous [Batch](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/batch.md) work, is not included. Streamed responses never include this header, because it is added after the response has been produced. For a streamed request, read the `cost` recorded with the conversation (available when conversation logging is enabled) or calculate the cost from the reported token counts. Use your account usage records as the source of truth for billing.

Parse the value as a floating-point number. Very small amounts, such as `1E-05`, can be written in scientific notation, and the sum of several charges can carry floating-point noise in its last digits.

## Data Sharing discount

Accounts that enable [Data Sharing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-sharing.md) receive a 10% discount on eligible RAG query-embedding usage and eligible reranking operations performed while sharing is enabled. Other services keep their regular prices.

## Plan multipliers

Usage rates are subject to the plan's inference tax:

| Plan | Inference tax | Daily ceiling on model inference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Free | +25% | $1.50 |
| Pro | +5% | $1.20 |
| Max | +2% | $1.00 |
| Ultimate | 0% | Not applicable |

For integrated-model inference, the tax is recorded as its own usage entry, `inference.commission`, under the model that served the request, so token entries show the model's rates. Once the day's `inference.commission` entries reach the ceiling, further model inference is charged at the model's rates only. The day runs from midnight to midnight in the America/Sao_Paulo time zone, and the count starts again at midnight.

Other services subject to the plan multiplier include it in their own rates, and those charges don't count toward the ceiling.

BYOK usage is not affected by inference taxes. Product pages state when a rate is exempt from the plan multiplier, as with image generation.

## Credit top-ups

Adding credits charges the amount you choose plus the payment processor fee. Only the amount you choose is added to your balance; fees are not. On Free, an AIVAX service fee of 5% of the amount, with a $0.20 minimum, is also added. Pro, Max, and Ultimate pay no AIVAX service fee. The dashboard shows each fee and the total before you confirm the payment.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.html

# Plans and Limits

AIVAX has four account plans: **Free**, **Pro**, **Max**, and **Ultimate**. The current plan controls model access, account and product rate limits, storage quota, retention periods, and included daily service allowances. Every plan limit is listed on this page; product pages link here instead of repeating the values.

For commercial subscription prices and plan packaging, use the [AIVAX pricing page](https://aivax.net/pricing). The same public list prices are available from [Plan list prices](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md#plan-list-prices).

An em dash (`—`) means the plan does not impose a limit, and `Not available` means the feature is unavailable on the plan. Model, gateway, provider, or product-specific limits may still apply. Limits that are the same on every plan, such as file sizes or results per request, are documented on each product page.

## Account limits

| Limit | Free | Pro | Max | Ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Inference** |  |  |  |  |
| Model access | Low-price models | All models | All models | All models |
| Inference commission multiplier | 1.25x | 1.05x | 1.02x | 1.00x |
| Daily inference commission ceiling | $1.50 | $1.20 | $1.00 | No commission |
| Integrated model requests | 20/min and 500/day | 150/min | 1,000/min | — |
| Integrated model input tokens | 1,000,000/min | 15,000,000/min | 60,000,000/min | — |
| BYOK requests | 30/min | 150/min | 1,000/min | — |
| Maximum context | 64,000 input tokens | — | — | — |
| LLM subscription coverage | Currently disabled | Currently disabled | Currently disabled | Currently disabled |
| **Account and support** |  |  |  |  |
| Storage quota | 30 MB | 2 GB | 10 GB | 20 GB |
| Cost per excess GB | Not available | $0.50/GB/month | $0.30/GB/month | $0.20/GB/month |
| Conversation retention | 2 hours | 2 days | 14 days | 30 days |
| RAG search history retention | 2 hours | 3 days | 14 days | 30 days |
| Service fee on credit top-ups | 5% (minimum $0.20) | None | None | None |
| Support level | Email | Priority | Priority | Dedicated |

Document text stored in a collection counts toward the storage quota as UTF-8 bytes. Text with accents or non-Latin characters can use more of that quota than basic Latin text of the same length. RAG search history is the list of searches shown in [RAG Observability](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/observability.md#search-history).

Integrated model requests are limited by both request count and input tokens. Model rate-limit groups adjust the request-count thresholds:

| Rate-limit group | Threshold multiplier |
| --- | --- |
| Common | 1.0x |
| Discounted | 0.5x |
| Low | 0.3x |
| Free | 0.1x |

For example, a Pro account normally has 150 integrated-model requests per minute. With a `Discounted` model group, the adjusted threshold is 75 requests per minute.

BYOK uses a provider key configured on the gateway instead of an integrated AIVAX model, but requests still pass through AIVAX infrastructure and use the plan's BYOK limit.

Rate limits are shared across all API keys of the same account. A request that would exceed an active window returns `429 Too Many Requests`; pace requests and use bounded retries with backoff.

Custom accounts use the Pro plan rate limits multiplied by a factor agreed for the account, or have no plan rate limits when no factor is set. Custom accounts support 8 concurrent Agentic Test runs.

## Product limits

Product limits use the same rules as account limits: they are shared across the account's API keys, and a request above an active window returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Where a limit counts items instead of HTTP requests, the note below its table says so.

### RAG and collections

| Limit | Free | Pro | Max | Ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collections | 5 | 100 | 1,000 | — |
| Searches | 20/min | 300/min | 1,500/min | 3,000/min |
| Reranking requests | 30/min | 500/min | 3,000/min | — |
| Reflex processing time | 30 minutes/day | 3 hours/day | 12 hours/day | — |
| Document insertions | 500/day | 5,000/day | 50,000/day | — |
| Documents per multipart JSONL import | 1,000 | 5,000 | 100,000 | 1,000,000 |
| Documents per WebSocket JSONL import | 10,000 | 50,000 | 1,000,000 | 10,000,000 |
| Media Injector files | 2/day | 20/day | 250/day | 1,000/day |

The reranking request limit applies to the [reranking endpoint](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reflex.md) and to RAG searches that use a reranker, including searches through AI Gateways and MCP tools. The Reflex processing-time limit counts the time spent processing Reflex requests on both paths; cached input does not consume it separately. If an import exceeds the per-import limit, split it into multiple imports. See [Collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md), [Documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md), and [Reflex](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reflex.md).

### Data processing

| Limit | Free | Pro | Max | Ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Text-classification documents | 30/min and 300/day | 500/min | 2,500/min | 10,000/min |
| Extraction, summarization, and instruction refinement documents | 10/min and 300/day | 100/min | 1,000/min | 2,500/min |
| Text-segmentation documents | 10/min and 100/day | 300/min | 1,000/min | 2,500/min |
| Translation requests | 30/min and 300/day | 100/min | 1,000/min | 2,500/min |
| Media description requests | 10/min and 30/hour | 40/min | 100/min | 200/min |
| Semantic decision requests | 10/min | 30/min | 200/min | — |

Classification, extraction, summarization, and segmentation limits count every item in the request's `documents` array, not each HTTP request; extraction and summarization share one quota. Instruction refinement shares that quota and counts every item in its `context` array. Translation, media description, and semantic decision limits count HTTP requests. A semantic decision request consumes one unit regardless of how many questions it contains or which decision model it selects, and included decision usage still consumes request units. See [Classification](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/classification.md), [Extraction](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/extraction.md), [Summarization](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/summarization.md), [Instruction Refinement](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/instruction-refinement.md), [Text segmentation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/text-segmentation.md), [Translations](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/translations.md), [Media descriptions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/media-descriptions.md), and [Semantic Decisions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/decisions.md).

### Speech

| Limit | Free | Pro | Max | Ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone text-to-speech requests | 3/min and 40/hour | 20/min | 100/min | 300/min |
| Standalone audio-transcription requests | 3/min and 40/hour | 20/min | 100/min | 300/min |

Text-to-speech and transcription have separate quotas with the same values. [Voice Sessions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/voice-session.md) are not subject to these standalone quotas. See [Text-to-speech](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/speech.md) and [Speech-to-text](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/audio-transcriptions.md).

### Built-in tools and web search

| Limit | Free | Pro | Max | Ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web search | 15/day | 500/day | 4,000/day | 10,000/day |
| X/Twitter search | Not available | 200/day | 3,000/day | 10,000/day |
| Document and web page generation | 5/day | 500/day | 15,000/day | 50,000/day |
| Image generation and editing | 5/day | 150/day | 1,500/day | 5,000/day |
| General service actions | 30/day | 2,500/day | 30,000/day | 100,000/day |
| Bash commands | 300/hour | 30,000/hour | 100,000/hour | — |

General service actions share one daily quota. The image generation limit is one daily quota shared by the built-in tool, the [image generation API](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/generations/images.md), and the [Media generation MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/media-generation-mcp.md); each request counts once, whatever the number of images it asks for. See [Built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md), [Web Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/web-foundation/web-search.md), and [Shell](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/shell.md).

### Batch and Agentic Tests

| Limit | Free | Pro | Max | Ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Batch workflow items processed | 500/day | 25,000/day | 250,000/day | — |
| New Agentic Test runs | 5/min | 20/min | 100/min | — |
| Concurrent Agentic Test runs | 1 | 4 | 6 | 8 |

If batch processing is paused because of quota, it resumes after the window resets. Manual runs, scheduled runs, and direct evaluations share one new-run quota. See [Batch](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/batch.md#limits) and [Agentic Tests](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/agentic-tests.md#pricing-and-limits).

## Included daily subscription allowances

Every plan includes separate daily allowances for the services below. Each comparison refers to the same service on the Free plan, not to a shared credit balance or a guaranteed number of requests. Unused allowance from one service cannot cover another. Custom accounts do not receive subscription allowances.

| Included service | Free | Pro | Max | Ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RAG search and insertion embeddings | 10,000 tokens | 15× Free | 50× Free | 100× Free |
| Reranking with Reflex | 2,000 input tokens | 4× Free | 20× Free | 50× Free |
| Semantic decisions with eligible models | 20,000 input tokens | 2× Free | 3× Free | 5× Free |
| Fetch and OCR extraction | 1,000 PUs | 8× Free | 25× Free | 50× Free |

RAG searches and document insertions share the embedding allowance. It does not cover answer generation, media processing, document extraction or summarization, text classification, or segmentation. A query embedding served from cache does not consume it. Reflex uses a separate reranking allowance that includes both cached and uncached input. The semantic decision allowance covers only eligible decision models; see [Semantic Decisions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/decisions.md#usage-and-cost). Optional Fetch JSON conversion is separate from the extraction allowance.

Coverage is evaluated for each metered service item: a document's embedding, an individual query-term embedding, a reranking call, a decision call's input usage, or an extraction operation. Each item is either fully included or billed in full at normal rates. Included items are tracked in subscription consumption, not as zero-cost entries in billing history. The current allowances permit a 10% margin above their base capacity. An item that would exceed that margin leaves the allowance unchanged and is billed normally. One request can contain several items, so some may be included while others are charged.

Daily allowances reset at midnight in the server's local time. Check the account's subscription usage indicators for consumption and reset status; usage can exceed 100% while within the margin. LLM subscription coverage is currently disabled, so text-model inference and RAG answer generation remain metered separately. Allowances do not bypass balance requirements or rate limits. See [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md) for how uncovered items are billed. For a walkthrough of testing a retrieval pipeline within these allowances, see [Free RAG API on AIVAX Free](https://aivax.net/blog/free-tier-for-rag-reflex-decisions-and-ocr/).

## Estimating PUs and tokens

Usage is metered in processing units (PUs) or tokens, depending on the service. The examples below help you estimate the size of a workload. They are approximations (`≈`), not guaranteed values: the exact amount is reported in each response's usage fields.

**Fetch and OCR processing units**

| Content | Approximate PUs |
| --- | --- |
| Plain text or Markdown file | 0 |
| Native-text PDF or DOCX, 10 pages | ≈ 1 (minimum of 1 PU per item) |
| Web page that renders in 1 to 3 seconds | ≈ 10–30 (10 PUs per second of rendering) |
| Photo or screenshot with text | ≈ 40–50 |
| Scanned PDF, 10 pages | ≈ 400–500 |

Native pages are converted from their text layer and cost almost nothing; scanned pages, images, and images embedded in a page go through OCR and drive the total. A PDF that mixes both is billed for the pages that actually need OCR.

**Tokens**

| Content | Approximate tokens |
| --- | --- |
| RAG search query, such as "how do I reset my password if I lost access to my email?" | ≈ 10–30 |
| One page of English text, about 500 words | ≈ 650–750 |
| RAG document chunk of 1,500 characters | ≈ 350–400 |
| Reflex reranking of 50 candidates with about 300 tokens each | ≈ 15,000–16,000, since the query is scored with every candidate |
| A 300-page book, about 300 words per page | ≈ 110,000–130,000 |

Token estimates assume English text, where one token is about four characters or three quarters of a word. Portuguese, Spanish, and other accented languages usually need 20–50% more tokens for the same content; code, JSON, and non-Latin scripts can need more. A query embedding served from cache is not billed, and in chat completions the conversation history and system instructions are sent again on every turn.

## Public API keys

Public keys have additional limits independent of the account plan.

| Scope | Request limits |
| --- | --- |
| Per remote address | 3/5s, 20/min, 300/hour, 1,000/day |
| Global per key | 10/5s, 60/min, 1,500/hour, 10,000/day |

| Scope | Token limits |
| --- | --- |
| Per remote address | 100,000/5min, 500,000/30min, 2,000,000/6h, 5,000,000/day |
| Global per key | 500,000/5min, 2,000,000/30min, 10,000,000/6h, 25,000,000/day |

Public keys can be used for chat completions, the `/api/v1/generations/*` endpoints, RAG semantic search, and RAG answer generation. For chat completions, public keys also require a full AI Gateway UUID, restrict request parameters, and omit server-side tool surfaces. See [Authentication](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/authentication.md).

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-sharing.html

# Data Sharing

AIVAX offers an optional semantic data collection program for accounts that choose to contribute eligible RAG and reranking data to model development. In exchange, eligible operations receive a discount. Document indexing and storage are outside this program. All collected RAG and reranking records are anonymized before they are written to the training dataset.

The setting is disabled by default. It must be enabled by an authorized Account Manager, meaning the person using the AIVAX account, not a role in the API.

## What changes when collection is enabled

While the setting is enabled:

- eligible RAG query-embedding usage receives a discount (see [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md#data-sharing-discount));
- eligible reranking operations receive the same discount; and
- document indexing, storage, unrelated inference, tools, and other services keep their regular prices.

The discount applies only to eligible operations performed while collection is enabled. Disabling collection removes the discount from future operations.

## Data included

Depending on the operation, AIVAX may collect:

| Operation | Collected data |
| --- | --- |
| RAG semantic search | Query terms, selected reranker, and the contents and relevance scores of returned documents. |
| Reranking | Query, submitted documents, selected reranker, and ranking results. Unknown response metadata and usage or billing information are not included. |

The anonymized dataset does not store the account ID, API key, request ID, collection or document IDs, document names, billing data, or collection timestamp. The account is consulted transiently only to verify that collection is enabled and to apply the eligible operation discount. Document indexing and stored collections are never copied into the training dataset by this program; document content is included only when it is submitted for reranking or returned by a RAG search.

Enabling this setting does not by itself include unrelated chat completions, conversations, tool calls, or other account resources in the training dataset.

## Purpose and use

AIVAX may use collected data to develop, train, fine-tune, evaluate, test, and improve models and systems related to embeddings, retrieval, ranking, reranking, and other semantic processing. This may include preparing datasets, annotating or transforming records, measuring quality, and producing aggregated or derived artifacts.

Access is limited to authorized personnel and service providers that support these purposes under applicable confidentiality and data-protection obligations. AIVAX does not sell collected semantic data or maintain an account-to-record mapping for this dataset.

## Account Manager responsibilities

In AIVAX legal terms, the Account Manager is the person using the AIVAX account. Before enabling collection, the Account Manager must:

- have authority to accept these conditions for the account;
- have an appropriate legal basis for AIVAX to use the submitted data for the purposes above;
- provide any notices and obtain any permissions or consents required from end users or other data subjects; and
- avoid submitting credentials, secrets, regulated data, or sensitive personal data unless its collection and use are legally permitted and necessary.

## Enabling, disabling, and deletion

The Account Manager can control collection in **Dashboard > My account > Semantic data collection**.

- The setting is disabled by default.
- Enabling it authorizes anonymized collection of future eligible RAG and reranking operations.
- Disabling it stops new collection and ends the discount for future operations.
- Disabling it does not automatically delete records collected while consent was active or reverse training already completed.

Because account identifiers and account-to-record mappings are not stored, AIVAX cannot retrieve or delete training records merely from an account ID. Requests concerning personal data present inside submitted semantic content can be sent to **privacy@aivax.net** or **wm@aivax.net**. Where applicable, include enough information to locate the content.

Source records are retained only for as long as reasonably necessary for the documented purposes, legal obligations, security, and audit requirements, and may then be deleted. Deletion of source records does not require AIVAX to retrain or destroy models or aggregated artifacts that no longer identify a person, except where required by applicable law.

See the [Privacy Policy](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/legal/privacy-policy.md) and [Terms of Use](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/legal/terms-of-service.md) for the governing legal terms.

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.html

# Collections

AIVAX provides a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) service for storing knowledge and retrieving it later through semantic search. A collection is an account-owned knowledge base: it groups the [documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md) that belong together and is the unit you search, attach to an AI Gateway, and maintain.

Compare vector storage with the surrounding ingestion and retrieval pipeline in [RAG vs vector database](https://aivax.net/blog/a-vector-database-is-not-a-rag-system/).

## When to create a collection

Use collections to separate knowledge that belongs to different knowledge bases, products, tenants, languages, or operational purposes. For example, a support collection can hold help-center answers, a legal collection can hold contract clauses, and a product collection can hold descriptions, policies, and troubleshooting notes.

Prefer several focused collections over one large collection when the content is searched by different audiences or applications. A search can include several collections at once, while a collection boundary keeps unrelated content out of results, simplifies maintenance, and keeps [advanced filters](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md) fast.

## What a collection contains

Each collection has:

- A unique collection ID.
- A name.
- Optional context and contextual tags.
- A set of documents and their indexing state.
- Usage statistics based on the searches performed on it.

The **collection context** describes the knowledge base to an AI Gateway when the collection is used for RAG, for example the audience, scope, and how the content should be used. Keep it durable and collection-wide; source-specific import guidance belongs in the import itself.

## Use a collection

After adding and indexing documents, you can:

- Search it directly with [Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md), optionally narrowed with [advanced filters](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md) and reordered with a [reranker](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md).
- Attach it to an [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md) so retrieved documents are placed into the model context automatically.
- Expose it to MCP clients through the [Collections and RAG MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/collections-mcp.md).
- Monitor its retrieval quality and search history in the Console; see [RAG Observability](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/observability.md).

## Maintain a collection

Collection settings in the Console also provide maintenance actions:

- **Update outdated documents** regenerates vectors for documents indexed with an embedding model that differs from the collection's current model. Regenerating vectors incurs document-embedding charges.
- **Reset collection** removes the collection's documents while keeping the collection itself.
- **Delete collection** removes the collection and its documents.

Reset and delete cannot be undone. Export the collection as JSONL through the API first when you may need its documents again.

## De-duplicator

The collection de-duplicator removes repeated documents from a collection. Use it after merging several sources, re-importing content under new document names, or generating documents with [Media Injector](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md#import-from-files-with-media-injector), when the same knowledge may exist more than once and crowd search results with near-identical matches.

Start it from the collection settings in the Console, under **Advanced settings > De-duplicate collection**, or through the API. Choose how aggressive the comparison should be:

| Level | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Low | Removes only exact duplicates and near-identical semantic documents. |
| Medium | Recommended default. Balances recall and safety. |
| High | More aggressive semantic matching; can remove documents that are only very similar. |

The de-duplicator runs in two passes. It first removes documents whose text is exactly the same, then compares indexed documents with their closest neighbors in the collection and removes those above the selected similarity level. One document of each duplicate group is kept. Documents still waiting for indexing are only compared in the exact pass, so wait for indexing to finish before running it.

Before starting, the Console shows an estimate of the processing units and cost for the current number of documents. The task runs in the background, and only one de-duplication can run per collection at a time. When it finishes or fails, the account receives a notification.

Removed documents are deleted, not hidden. Before deleting them, AIVAX backs them up as JSONL files with their name, text, reference, and tags, and the completion notification links to these backups. Metadata is not included in the backup, so export the collection first when document metadata matters.

The de-duplicator is billed by processing time: one processing unit (PU) per second of processing, with a minimum of one PU per task. The plan multiplier applies.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Estimate%20Collection%20De-duplication)

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Start%20Collection%20De-duplication)

## Manage collections through the API

Collections can be created, listed, inspected, edited, reset, exported, and deleted through the API. See the [API reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs) for the Collections endpoints.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Create%20Collection)

## Pricing and limits

Indexing and search are billed by token usage. Generated RAG answers are charged separately from query embedding, and their price varies with the summarization model. The plan multiplier applies.

| Description | Pricing |
| --- | ---: |
| Collection text embedding | **$0.015/M tokens** |
| Search - query cache miss | **$0.015/M tokens** |
| Search - query cache hit | Zero |
| RAG answer generation | **~$0.50/M tokens**, excluding query rates |
| Collection de-duplication | **$0.05/1k PUs** |

Every plan includes a daily embedding allowance shared by searches and document insertions; see [Included daily subscription allowances](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#included-daily-subscription-allowances). Accounts with [Data Sharing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-sharing.md) enabled receive a discount on eligible query embeddings. Reranking and [Reflex](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reflex.md#pricing-and-limits) are billed separately.

The number of collections, searches, reranking requests, and document insertions depends on the plan; see [RAG and collections limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#rag-and-collections). Requests above a limit return `429 Too Many Requests`.

# Documents

A document is the unit that AIVAX indexes and retrieves inside a [collection](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md). Each document stores text, an optional reference, optional tags, optional metadata, and the vectors generated by the indexing job. Search quality depends heavily on how clear, focused, and self-contained each document is.

## Anatomy of a document

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Required stable identifier, up to 256 characters. Existing documents are matched by name, so reuse the same name to update a document. |
| Contents | Required text that is embedded and searched semantically. |
| Reference | Optional ID, up to 64 characters, that groups chunks belonging to the same logical source. |
| Tags | Optional labels for filtering, browsing, and maintenance. |
| Metadata | Optional object returned with results, such as source URL, version, author, or publication date. |

Only the contents are embedded. Metadata and tags are returned with results and can be used in [advanced filters](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md), but they do not influence semantic matching. If users may search for "refund policy", those words must appear in the contents, not only in a tag.

Use references when several documents represent parts of the same source, such as sections of a contract, clauses of a policy, or chunks of a PDF. When a search enables reference expansion, a matched document can bring the other documents that share its reference.

## Write good documents

A document should represent one limited piece of knowledge. As a practical target, keep most documents between 20 and 700 words. This is not an API rule, but it usually gives the embedding model enough context without mixing unrelated topics. Split longer content at logical boundaries such as sections, clauses, FAQ entries, or product descriptions.

Do:

- Give each document a clear name and focused text.
- Put the subject near the start of the document.
- Use natural language similar to the way users ask questions.
- Repeat important identifiers, product names, policy names, acronyms, and terms when they matter.
- Include enough context for the text to be understood on its own.

Avoid:

- Empty, tiny, or title-only documents.
- Entire PDFs, chapters, logs, or manuals as one document.
- Multiple unrelated subjects in one document.
- Text that depends on surrounding pages to make sense.
- Mixed languages inside the same document, unless users are expected to search that way.
- Raw JSON, code, tables, or logs without a short natural-language explanation.
- Pronouns such as "it" or "the product" when the document does not identify the subject.

For example, prefer:

```text
The color of the 2015 Honda Civic registered in fleet record CAR-123 is yellow.
```

over:

```text
The car is yellow.
```

The first version can be retrieved and understood without external context.

### Chunking larger sources

When importing PDFs, spreadsheets, web pages, or manuals, inspect the resulting chunks before relying on the collection. Remove repeated headers, footers, navigation menus, broken tables, boilerplate, and irrelevant disclaimers when possible.

A good chunk includes a title or source heading, the immediate section context, and the complete rule, answer, or explanation. A poor chunk contains half of a table row, a sentence that depends on the previous page, or several policies mixed together.

[Text Segmentation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/text-segmentation.md) can split source text into cohesive segments before import. For an end-to-end script that converts a PDF with Fetch, segments it, and writes JSONL with stable `docid` values, see [how to convert a PDF to Markdown for RAG and split it into chunks](https://aivax.net/blog/pdf-to-markdown-for-rag-chunks-jsonl/).

### Document size

Very small documents, below about 32 tokens, are accepted but may not be retrieved reliably.
