Documents above about 4,096 tokens are accepted and indexed, but they record a warning in the account logs because a single vector represents their whole text less precisely. Text far beyond that size is truncated for embedding. Split large documents instead of relying on truncation.

## Import documents

AIVAX supports several ways to add documents. All of them queue new or changed documents for indexing; a document becomes searchable after its state changes from **Queued** to **Indexed**.

| Method | Use when |
| --- | --- |
| Create or update one document | Your application manages documents one at a time, such as an admin screen that saves one FAQ entry. |
| Batch import over WebSocket | You have many prepared documents, such as chunks generated from PDFs, catalogs, policies, or help-center articles. |
| Import from files with Media Injector | You have source files whose knowledge has not yet been split into retrieval-ready text. |

### Updates and reindexing

Documents are matched by name. When a document is created, it is queued for indexing. When its contents change, it is queued again and its vectors are regenerated. Unchanged documents are skipped.

What you can update without changing the contents depends on the import method:

- **Single-document update:** changes the reference, tags, or metadata without reindexing. Fields you omit keep their current values.
- **Batch import:** updates metadata alone without reindexing. The reference and tags are updated only together with changed contents, so a line that changes only the reference or tags is skipped.

> [!WARNING]
> Indexing incurs cost based on document text tokens when documents are created or when their contents change.

### Batch import

Use the **Index Documents (JSONL WebSocket)** endpoint for batch imports. It replaces the multipart **Index Documents (JSONL)** upload, which remains available only for existing integrations. The WebSocket import streams documents in blocks, reports progress as it goes, accepts 10× the per-request document limit of the multipart upload, and lets you resume from the last committed line after a disconnection.

Each JSONL line represents one document:

| Property | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docid` | Yes | Document name. Existing documents are matched by this value. |
| `text` | Yes | Contents to index. |
| `__ref` | No | Reference ID. |
| `__tags` | No | Tags. See [RAG metadata filtering](https://aivax.net/blog/filter-rag-results-by-metadata-tags-date/) for how tags, metadata, and dates pre-filter search results. |
| `__meta` | No | Metadata object. |

The import works as follows:

1. Open a WebSocket to the endpoint. Browsers can authenticate with the `api-key` query parameter. Add `insert-mode=sync` to delete collection documents whose names were not sent.
2. Send UTF-8 text messages with complete JSONL lines separated by `\n`. A message can contain one or many lines. Each message must arrive within 30 seconds of the previous one.
3. AIVAX commits the lines in blocks. For each block it checks the account balance, storage quota, and collection access, saves the documents, queues them for indexing, and sends a `progress` message with the number of committed lines.
4. Send a line containing only `END`. AIVAX saves the remaining lines, applies `insert-mode=sync` when requested, and sends a `completed` message before closing the connection.

If the connection closes, times out, or fails before `END`, uncommitted lines are discarded, while committed blocks remain queued. The `error` message reports the committed line count, so you can resend only the remaining lines. Only one import runs per collection at a time; a second import waits up to 30 seconds and then fails with `409 Conflict`.

When a line changes the text of an existing document, its reference and tags are replaced by the values sent; an omitted `__meta` keeps the existing metadata.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Index%20Documents%20(JSONL%20WebSocket))

### Import from files with Media Injector

Media Injector turns a source file into focused, self-contained documents. It examines the source, identifies materially useful knowledge, writes concise factual documents in the source's predominant language, and queues them for indexing. Use direct import instead when you need exact source wording, deterministic boundaries, stable document names, or application-controlled metadata.

Media Injector is useful for PDFs that contain several independent topics, images or scanned pages whose visible content should become searchable, and audio or video whose facts should be available through RAG. It does not preserve the source as one searchable document. Review the generated documents when wording, coverage, legal fidelity, or sensitive-data handling is important.

In the Console:

1. Open the target collection and choose **Import from files**.
2. Select one or more source files.
3. Optionally provide processing context. The same context is applied to every selected file.
4. Confirm the import. The files are uploaded sequentially, and a separate job is created for each file after all of its chunks have reached AIVAX.
5. Follow the jobs under **Batch > Media Processing**.
6. After each job completes, review the generated documents and wait for indexing before testing [Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md).

A job can be `queued`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. Failed or cancelled jobs can be retried while their uploaded data is still available.

If no job appears, the upload did not reach its completion step. Retry the upload and check the error shown. File names are preserved during upload, including accented letters and non-Latin scripts.

| Source group | Processing behavior |
| --- | --- |
| PDF documents | Reads document structure, text, and relevant visual content. |
| Images | Interprets visible text and content. |
| Audio | Interprets spoken and other relevant audible content; large files are segmented automatically. |
| Video | Interprets relevant visual and audible content; large files are segmented automatically. |

Use the original, accurate file extension, because it identifies the media type. If an audio or video file fails, convert it to a common format and retry.

**Processing context** is an optional instruction that helps Media Injector decide which facts are most valuable. It is not treated as a factual source and cannot add facts that are absent from the file. Describe the source's identity and purpose, the audience, the topics that matter, ambiguous terminology, and content to deprioritize:

```text
This is the 2026 support policy for Acme Cloud customers in Brazil. Prioritize eligibility rules, deadlines, plan differences, exceptions, and the steps a support agent must communicate. Ignore repeated page headers and signature blocks.
```

Do not ask it to infer conclusions, supply missing information, or calculate values the source does not report.

Generated documents:

- Prioritize source identity, scope, principal facts, relationships, and exceptions.
- Combine closely related facts.
- Ignore decorative text and pagination.
- Preserve the source's language, terminology, dates, and number formats.
- Are tagged as automatically produced content and indexed like other documents.

Inspect documents generated from tables, scans, and repeated layouts before relying on them in production. For a sampling procedure that grades each generated document against facts you wrote down beforehand, see [how to check PDF and scan ingestion quality before you embed for RAG](https://aivax.net/blog/check-pdf-ingestion-quality-before-embedding-for-rag/).

## Manage documents

You can manage documents in the Console, on the collection's **Browse documents** tab, or through the API. Management capabilities include:

- **Browse and filter** by tag, reference, content, name, or ID, by indexing state (queued or indexed), and sorted by creation, update, or indexing date.
- **Inspect** a document's contents, reference, tags, metadata, timestamps, and approximate token count. The Console editor also warns when a document has too many or too few words.
- **Edit** contents, reference, tags, and metadata. Changing the contents reindexes the document.
- **Delete** individual documents, or remove documents that were not sent in a synchronized batch import with `insert-mode=sync`.
- **Export** all documents of a collection as JSONL.
- **Remove duplicates** with the [collection de-duplicator](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md#de-duplicator).

See the Documents and Collections groups of the [API reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs) for the endpoints, including **Create or Update Document**, **Browse Documents**, **Get Document**, **Delete Document**, and **Export Collection**.

## Troubleshoot retrieval

When search results are poor, check the basics first:

- Confirm the documents are indexed.
- Test the collection with [Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md) or the Console playground before testing through an AI Gateway.
- Try a complete question instead of isolated keywords, and compare the query language with the document language.
- Review whether the answer is split across too many small documents or buried inside a very large one.
- Check search history and query coverage in [RAG Observability](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/observability.md).

## Pricing and limits

Document indexing is billed as collection text embedding; see [Collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md#pricing-and-limits). Media Injector is billed for input, cached input, output, and media usage of the processing job, in addition to the normal embedding cost of the generated documents. Rates depend on media type and input-token volume.

| Media Injector | Pricing |
| --- | ---: |
| PDFs and images - up to 272K input tokens | Input **$0.30/M tokens**; cache **$0.03/M tokens**; output **$1.80/M tokens** |
| PDFs and images - above 272K input tokens | Input **$0.60/M tokens**; cache **$0.06/M tokens**; output **$3.60/M tokens** |
| Audio - up to 256K input tokens | Input/media **$0.60/M tokens**; cache **$0.12/M tokens**; output **$3.00/M tokens** |
| Audio - above 256K input tokens | Input/media **$1.20/M tokens**; cache **$0.24/M tokens**; output **$6.00/M tokens** |
| Video | Input/media **$0.45/M tokens**; cache **$0.045/M tokens**; output **$3.75/M tokens** |

Daily document insertions, documents per JSONL import, and daily Media Injector files depend on the plan; see [RAG and collections limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#rag-and-collections). If an import exceeds the per-import limit, split it into multiple imports. If the account reaches the daily insertion limit, wait for the window to reset or upgrade the plan.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.html

# Search

Search returns indexed documents from one or more collections. Use managed search when AIVAX should store and search a persistent corpus, or when the corpus is too large to submit as candidates with every request.

AIVAX searches through three endpoints:

| Endpoint | Path | Use it to | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Query collections | `POST /api/v2/query` | Find the documents that best answer a question. | Query embedding and, when used, reranking. |
| Find similar documents | `POST /api/v2/query/similar` | Find documents close in meaning to a document you already have. | No embedding or reranking cost. |
| Browse documents | `POST /api/v2/query/browse` | List documents in a fixed order, optionally filtered, without relevance. | No embedding or reranking cost. |

RAG answer generation and collections attached to an AI Gateway use the same retrieval engine.

If your application already owns the candidate document strings, consider [Reflex](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reflex.md). Reflex is a collection-less search that ranks supplied documents without indexing or storage.

Before searching:

1. Add [documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md) to a [collection](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md).
2. Wait for indexing. Only indexed documents are returned.
3. Compare [vector search with the complete RAG pipeline](https://aivax.net/blog/a-vector-database-is-not-a-rag-system/) before deciding what to build.

## Query collections

Use this endpoint to find the documents that best answer a question.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Query%20collections)

A query runs in this order:

1. If a filter is set, AIVAX restricts each collection to the documents that match it.
2. Each search term is embedded and compared with the remaining documents.
3. Documents below `minScore` are discarded, and the closest `candidates` documents form the candidate pool.
4. The reranker reorders the pool, unless reranking is disabled.
5. The pool is sorted and returned in pages of `limit` results.

```json
{
  "collections": [ "<collection-id>" ],
  "terms": "How do I request a refund?"
}
```

Use these options to narrow the corpus, size the pool, and page the results.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `collections` | Required | Collection IDs owned by the account. An item can also be `{ "id": "<collection-id>", "filter": "..." }` to filter only that collection. |
| `terms` | Required | One search text or a list of alternative texts. |
| `filter` | — | An [advanced filter](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md) expression, or a list of expressions that must all match. |
| `minScore` | 0.2 | Minimum vector similarity, from 0 to 0.99, for a document to enter the candidate pool. Raise it to drop weak matches; lower it when relevant documents are missing. |
| `candidates` | `limit` × 3 | Size of the candidate pool, from `limit` to 1000. A larger pool gives the reranker and later pages more documents to work with. |
| `reranker` | `smart` (Reflex) | Reranker that orders the pool: `smart`, `lexical`, `rrf`, `none`, or a full reranker name. See [Rerankers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md). |
| `sort` | Score, descending | `{ "by": "score" \| "createdAt" \| "updatedAt" \| "indexedAt" \| "name", "dir": "asc" \| "desc" }`. Without `dir`, score sorts descending and the other fields ascending. |
| `limit` | 10 | Results per page, from 1 to 128. |
| `cursor` | — | `page.cursor` from the previous response, to read the next page. |
| `include` | `content`, `metadata` | Optional document fields: `content`, `metadata`, and `references`. `references` attaches the other documents that share the reference of each result. |

### Sorting and reranking

Use this table when you need to know whether a reranker runs. A reranker orders by relevance, so it only applies when results are sorted by score:

| Request | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| No `sort` and no `reranker` | Reflex reranks the pool; results are sorted by score. |
| `reranker` without `sort` | That reranker reranks the pool; results are sorted by score. |
| `sort` other than score, without `reranker` | Reranking is disabled. The pool is selected by similarity and then sorted by the requested field. |
| `sort` other than score with `reranker: "none"` | Same as above. |
| `sort` other than score with any other `reranker` | Rejected with `400 Bad Request`. |

To get the most recent relevant documents, select a pool by meaning and sort it by date:

```json
{
  "collections": [ "<collection-id>" ],
  "terms": "pricing change",
  "candidates": 100,
  "sort": { "by": "createdAt", "dir": "desc" }
}
```

Each reranker has a maximum number of documents it accepts; a `candidates` value above it is rejected.

### Results

Each result tells you which document matched and how it scored. It has a `rank`, a `document`, and `scores`:

- `document` contains `id`, `collectionId`, `name`, `reference`, `tags`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `indexedAt`, and the fields requested in `include`.
- `scores.similarity` is the vector similarity, `scores.rerank` is the reranker score (or `null`), and `scores.final` is the rerank score when a reranker ran, otherwise the similarity.

The response also contains `page.cursor`, `page.hasMore`, `page.candidates` (the size of the pool), and the `reranker` that ran.

### Pages

Use a cursor when the first page is not enough and you want the next slice of the same pool.

1. The first request computes the candidate pool and returns its first page.
2. To read the next page, send the same request body with `cursor` set to the previous `page.cursor`.
3. Later pages are read from the stored pool, so they are not charged again and keep the same order.

A cursor expires after 10 minutes without use and then returns `410 Gone`. Repeat the request without `cursor` to run the query again. A cursor sent with a different request body is rejected with `400 Bad Request`. The pool never grows. To see more than `candidates` results, raise `candidates`.

## Find similar documents

Use this endpoint for a "more like this" feature. It searches with the stored vector of an indexed document you already have.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Find%20similar%20documents)

The source document is never returned. The request accepts `documentId` and the same `collections`, `filter`, `minScore`, `candidates`, `sort`, `limit`, `cursor`, and `include` options as a query. Without `collections`, it searches the collection of the source document.

```json
{
  "documentId": "<document-id>",
  "limit": 5
}
```

Nothing is embedded or reranked.

- `scores.rerank` is always `null`.
- The source document must be indexed.
- A document still waiting for indexing is rejected with `400 Bad Request`.

## Browse documents

Use this endpoint to list indexed documents in a fixed order, without ranking by meaning.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Browse%20documents)

By default, documents are returned in insertion order, oldest first. Without a filter, every indexed document of the collections is listed.

```json
{
  "collections": [ "<collection-id>" ],
  "filter": "createdAt >= now-7d",
  "sort": { "by": "createdAt", "dir": "desc" },
  "limit": 50
}
```

It accepts `collections`, `filter`, `sort`, `limit`, `cursor`, and `include`.

- `sort.by` can be `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `indexedAt`, or `name`.
- Sorting by score is rejected.
- Results contain only `document`, without `rank` or `scores`.

Browse cursors point to the last returned document instead of a stored pool, so they do not expire. Documents added or changed between requests appear in later pages according to the sort order.

## Filter results

Filters narrow the documents a search can return, using exact conditions on document fields rather than semantic similarity. Use them when the answer must come from a known subset, such as one product, tenant, language, document type, or period.

| Filter on | Example | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | `name startswith "policy-"` | Document families that follow a naming convention. |
| Tags | `tags has "finance"` | Operational labels assigned on import. |
| Metadata | `metadata.region = "br"` | Structured values stored with each document, such as region, version, or author. |
| Contents | `content contains "refund"` | Required words or identifiers in the text. |
| Dates | `updatedAt >= now-30d` | Recently created or updated documents. |

How filters combine:

- Combine conditions with `and`, `or`, `not`, and parentheses, for example `tags has "finance" and createdAt >= now-30d`.
- When `filter` is a list, every expression must match.
- A filter set on a collection item is combined with the top-level `filter` for that collection.
- Filters run before the search terms are embedded.
- Only matching documents are ranked, so results never include documents outside the filter.
- When no document matches, a query returns an empty result without generating embeddings or charging for the query.

Filters do not replace good document text. The meaning a user searches for must appear in the contents. See [Advanced filters](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md) for the complete syntax, operators, limits, and errors, or [How to filter RAG results by metadata, tags and date](https://aivax.net/blog/filter-rag-results-by-metadata-tags-date/) for a worked guide.

## Multiple terms

Use multiple terms for synonyms, alternative phrasings, or several acceptable ways to find an answer. They cover alternative retrieval paths. They do not require every term to match the same document. Each document is scored by its best match among the terms.

If the user's question combines several related conditions, keep them together in one search term. Prefer:

```text
How do I cancel an annual subscription without a penalty?
```

Do not split that question into disconnected keywords:

```text
cancellation
annual subscription
penalty
```

A complete query usually performs better than a list of disconnected keywords because it preserves the relationship between concepts. If users search by product codes, policy IDs, plan names, or procedure names, include those identifiers in the document text.

## Reranking

Use a reranker when vector search already returned a candidate pool and you want a more relevant order. It adjusts that order. It does not search additional documents or recover text that the retrieval stage did not select. Raise `candidates` to give it more documents. See [Rerankers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md) for selection guidance.

## Errors

Use this table to match a failed search to the next action.

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid field, unknown collection or document, [invalid filter](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md#errors), a reranker combined with a sort other than score, or a cursor sent with a different request body. |
| `410 Gone` | The query cursor expired. Repeat the request without `cursor`. |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | The plan's search or reranking rate limit was exceeded. |

## Search quality

Use this checklist when search returns poor results:

1. Confirm that the documents are indexed.
2. Query the collection directly before testing through an AI Gateway.
3. Compare complete questions with alternative phrasings.
4. Check whether the relevant document is too short, too long, or not self-contained; see [Write good documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md#write-good-documents).
5. Check whether the query language matches the document language.
6. If the gateway rewrites questions before searching, test with the plain query path to isolate rewriting issues.
7. Review low-scoring searches and query coverage in [RAG Observability](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/observability.md).

To expose collections as tools for an external MCP client, see [Collections and RAG MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/collections-mcp.md). For search pricing and rate limits, see [Collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md#pricing-and-limits).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.html

# Advanced Filters

An advanced filter, also called a document filter, restricts a RAG search to the documents that match a condition, such as a tag, a metadata value, or a date range. Only documents that pass the filter are ranked by semantic similarity, so results never include documents outside the filter. For a task-oriented walkthrough, see [How to filter RAG results by metadata, tags and date](https://aivax.net/blog/filter-rag-results-by-metadata-tags-date/).

Filters are evaluated **before** the search terms are embedded. When no document in the requested collections matches the filter, the request returns an empty result without generating embeddings or charging for the search.

Some example filters:

```text
tags has "finance"
metadata.department = "finance" and createdAt >= now-30d
(tags has "finance" or tags has "legal") and not tags has "draft"
```

## Anatomy of a Filter

A filter is one or more **conditions** joined by `and`, `or`, and `not`. Every condition has three parts:

```text
metadata.pages   >   10
└── field ──┘   └op┘ └value┘
```

- **Field** — what to look at: `name`, `content`, `reference`, `tags`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or `metadata.<key>`. See [Fields](#fields).
- **Operator** — how to compare: `=`, `>`, `contains`, `in`, `has`, `exists`, and others. See [Operators](#operators).
- **Value** — a literal to compare against: a quoted string, a number, `true`, `false`, `null`, a date, or a list in parentheses. See [Values](#values).

The value must always be a literal. Functions, arithmetic, type conversions, and comparisons between two fields are not supported. Keywords, operators, and field names are case-insensitive: `AND`, `And`, and `and` are equivalent.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | text | The document name (`docid` in JSONL imports). |
| `content` | text | The indexed document text. |
| `reference` | text | The document reference that groups related documents, such as chunks of one source. Documents without a reference never match a positive condition on it. |
| `tags` | list of text | The document tags (`__tags`). |
| `createdAt` | date and time | When the document was created. |
| `updatedAt` | date and time | When the document was last updated. |
| `metadata.<key>` | JSON value | A value inside the document metadata (`__meta`). |

See [Documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md#anatomy-of-a-document) for how these fields are set.

## Operators

Each operator works only with specific fields and value types. Any other combination, such as `tags = "x"` or `name > "a"`, is rejected.

### Equality

| Operator | Meaning | Fields | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `=` | Equals | `name`, `content`, `reference`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `metadata.<key>` | `name = "refund-policy"` |
| `!=` | Not equals; exactly `not field = value` | Same as `=` | `metadata.lang != "en"` |

For `metadata.<key>`, the value may be text, a number, `true`, `false`, or `null`. Text comparison ignores letter case and accents; see [Strings](#strings).

### Ordering

| Operator | Meaning | Fields | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `>` `>=` `<` `<=` | Greater or less than | `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, numeric `metadata.<key>` | `metadata.pages > 10` |

Ordering works on dates for `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, and on **numbers only** for metadata. Dates or text stored in metadata cannot be ordered; see [Metadata](#metadata).

### Text

| Operator | Meaning | Fields | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contains` | Includes the text; at least 3 characters | `name`, `content`, `reference`, text `metadata.<key>` | `content contains "late fee"` |
| `startswith` | Begins with the text | Same | `name startswith "contract-"` |
| `endswith` | Ends with the text | Same | `name endswith ".pdf"` |

These operators match literally, without wildcards: `%` and `_` match only themselves. They do not split words or match synonyms. Use the search terms for meaning and the filter for exact constraints.

### Lists

| Operator | Meaning | Fields | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in` | Equals any value in the list | `name`, `content`, `reference`, `tags`, `metadata.<key>` | `metadata.region in ("latam", "emea")` |
| `has` | The list contains the value | `tags`, array `metadata.<key>` | `tags has "finance"` |

`field in (a, b, c)` is equivalent to `field = a or field = b or field = c`. For `tags`, `in` matches documents that have at least one of the listed tags. `has` is the only equality-style operator for `tags`; `tags = "x"` is rejected.

### Existence

| Operator | Meaning | Fields | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exists` | The metadata key is present, even when its value is `null` | `metadata.<key>` | `metadata.reviewer exists` |

`exists` takes no value. To require a non-null value, combine it with `!=`: `metadata.reviewer exists and metadata.reviewer != null`.

## Values

### Strings

Strings use double or single quotes. Inside a string, escape the same quote with a backslash: `"say \"hi\""`, `'it\'s'`. Supported escapes are `\"`, `\'`, `\\`, `\/`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, and `\uXXXX`.

Text comparisons ignore letter case and accents: `name = "relatorio"` matches a document named `Relatório`. `=` and `in` also ignore trailing spaces: `"report "` matches `"report"`.

### Numbers

Numbers use a dot as the decimal separator and may use an exponent: `10`, `-2.5`, `1e3`. Numbers are never quoted; `"100"` is a string.

### Booleans and null

`true`, `false`, and `null` are literals, written without quotes. They are valid only for `metadata.<key>`.

### Dates

`createdAt` and `updatedAt` accept absolute dates and relative times.

**Absolute dates** use ISO 8601 inside quotes:

```text
createdAt >= "2026-09-01"
updatedAt < "2026-09-01T18:30"
createdAt >= "2026-09-01T00:00:00-03:00"
createdAt >= "2026-09-01T03:00:00Z"
```

- A date without a time means midnight.
- A value without `Z` or an offset is interpreted in the AIVAX service time zone, America/Sao_Paulo (UTC−03:00). Add `Z` or an offset when you need an exact instant.
- Other formats, such as `15/06/2025`, are rejected.

**Relative times** use `now`, optionally followed by `+` or `-` and an amount with a unit, without quotes:

| Unit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `m` | minutes |
| `h` | hours |
| `d` | days |
| `w` | weeks |
| `mo` | calendar months |
| `y` | calendar years |

```text
createdAt >= now-7d
updatedAt >= now-12h and updatedAt < now
```

`now` is valid only in date conditions.

### Lists

A list is one or more values separated by commas inside parentheses: `("finance", "legal")`, `(2026, "2026")`. Lists are used with `in`.

## Combining Conditions

Join conditions with `and`, `or`, and `not`:

```text
not tags has "draft"
tags has "finance" and createdAt >= now-30d
(tags has "finance" or tags has "legal") and updatedAt >= "2026-01-01"
```

`not` binds tighter than `and`, and `and` binds tighter than `or`. So `a or b and c` means `a or (b and c)`. Use parentheses to group explicitly.

## Metadata

Use a dot to read nested metadata. Keys that are not simple identifiers go in quotes:

```text
metadata.author.name = "Ana"
metadata."file-path" startswith "/contracts/2026/"
metadata."a.b" = 1
```

The last example reads one key named `a.b`, not a nested path. Array indexes are not supported; use `has` to check whether an array contains a value.

**Types are never converted.** The literal type selects which stored values can match:

| Literal | Matches stored values of type |
| --- | --- |
| text | JSON string |
| number | JSON number |
| `true` / `false` | JSON boolean |
| `null` | JSON `null` |

So `metadata.year = 2026` does not match `{"year": "2026"}`, and `metadata.public = true` does not match `{"public": "true"}`. If your data mixes types, list both: `metadata.year in (2026, "2026")`.

Ordering operators work only on numbers in metadata. Dates stored in metadata cannot be compared as dates; use `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, or store a sortable number such as a Unix timestamp or `20260915`.

A missing key never matches a positive condition, so `metadata.lang != "en"` also matches documents without `lang`. To exclude them, add `metadata.lang exists`.

Store metadata with consistent types per key, and prefer keys made of ASCII letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

## Examples

| Goal | Filter |
| --- | --- |
| Documents with a tag | `tags has "finance"` |
| Any of several tags | `tags in ("finance", "legal")` |
| Exclude drafts | `not tags has "draft"` |
| A specific document | `name = "refund-policy"` |
| Documents from one family | `name startswith "manual-v2-"` |
| All chunks of one source | `reference = "manual-v2"` |
| Content mentioning a term | `content contains "late fee"` |
| Created in the last 30 days | `createdAt >= now-30d` |
| Updated in September 2026 | `updatedAt >= "2026-09-01" and updatedAt < "2026-10-01"` |
| One metadata value | `metadata.department = "finance"` |
| Several metadata values | `metadata.author.name in ("Ana", "Bruno")` |
| Numeric range | `metadata.pages > 10 and metadata.pages <= 200` |
| Boolean flag | `metadata.public = true` |
| Metadata array contains | `metadata.languages has "pt-BR"` |
| Key present and not null | `metadata.reviewer exists and metadata.reviewer != null` |
| Key absent | `not metadata.archived exists` |
| Combined | `(tags has "finance" or metadata.department = "finance") and createdAt >= now-1mo` |

## Common Mistakes

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| `name == "x"` | `name = "x"` |
| `lower(name) = "x"` | `name = "x"` (already case-insensitive) |
| `tags = "x"` | `tags has "x"` |
| `metadata.price > "100"` | `metadata.price > 100`, with the price stored as a number |
| `createdAt >= "15/06/2025"` | `createdAt >= "2025-06-15"` |
| `metadata.date >= "2025-06-15"` | `createdAt >= "2025-06-15"`, or a numeric metadata value |
| `content contains "ai"` | A term with at least 3 characters |
| `"filters": [ ... ]` | `"filter": [ ... ]` |

## Where Filters Are Supported

Send the filter in the `filter` field of these endpoints:

- [Query collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md#query-collections), [Find similar documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md#find-similar-documents), and [Browse documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md#browse-documents)
- Answer generation (see the endpoint reference below)

The field accepts a string or an array of strings. Array items are combined with `and`:

```json
{
  "terms": "How do I request a refund?",
  "collections": [ "<collection-id>" ],
  "filter": [
    "tags has \"billing\"",
    "metadata.region = \"latam\""
  ]
}
```

The search endpoints also accept a filter for a single collection, combined with the top-level `filter` for that collection:

```json
{
  "terms": "How do I request a refund?",
  "collections": [
    "<collection-id>",
    { "id": "<other-collection-id>", "filter": "metadata.source = \"crm\"" }
  ],
  "filter": "tags has \"billing\""
}
```

A missing or `null` field means no filter. The field name is `filter`; other names, such as `filters`, are ignored and the search runs without a filter.

Models can also send a filter string in the optional `filter` argument of these tools:

- The search tool of the [Collections MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/collections-mcp.md#generated-tools).
- The `query` tool of AI gateways that use the `QueryFunction` [query strategy](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md#rag).

The [`memory_search` tool](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md#search-memories) also accepts a filter string, but requires exactly one of `query` or `filter`, not both. Its filter-only mode returns up to 10 matching memories for the current user, newest first, without query embeddings.

Automatic gateway RAG, which searches before the model call, does not apply filters. An invalid filter in a tool call is returned to the model as a tool error with the same message as the API.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Query%20collections)

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Answer%20generation)

## Limits

These limits apply to every filter, including filters used by memory search and the Collections MCP.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Filter length | 2,048 characters per string |
| Conditions | 32 per string |
| Nesting of parentheses and `not` | 8 levels |
| Values in one `in` list | 100 |
| Length of a text value or metadata key | 256 characters |
| Keys in a metadata path | 8 |
| Minimum `contains` length | 3 characters |
| Execution time | 10 seconds |

Conditions on `content`, `endswith`, and tags examine every document in the requested collections, so they take longer in large collections. Metadata conditions use an index of metadata values and stay fast in large collections. If a filter exceeds the time limit, the request fails and asks for more selective conditions. To keep filters fast:

- Prefer conditions on `name` (`=`, `in`, `startswith`).
- Split very large corpora into smaller collections.
- Reserve `content contains` for collections where it stays fast.

## Errors

An invalid filter returns `400 Bad Request` with a message that names the problem and the character position where it was found:

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid filter: Unknown field 'author'. Expected name, content, reference, tags, createdAt, updatedAt or metadata.<key>. (at 0)"
}
```

For an array, the message includes the index of the invalid item, such as `Invalid filter at index 1: ...`. A `filter` that is not a string or an array of strings is also rejected.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/observability.html

# RAG Observability

The [AIVAX Console](https://console.aivax.net) shows how your collections are indexed, which searches they receive, and how well those searches score. Use it to confirm that an import finished, find questions your knowledge base answers poorly, and spot content that is never retrieved.

## Collections overview

Open **RAG Collections** in the Console sidebar. Each collection shows its **Current state** as a bar with three parts:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Indexed | Documents that are searchable with the collection's current embedding model. |
| Queued | Documents waiting for indexing. They are not searchable yet. |
| Outdated | Documents indexed with a different embedding model than the collection's current one. They remain searchable, but their vectors may be less accurate. |

A large Queued share after an import is normal and decreases as indexing proceeds. If Outdated documents remain, use **Update outdated documents** in the collection settings to regenerate their vectors; see [Maintain a collection](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md#maintain-a-collection).

## Collection health

Select **View** on a collection to open its **Browse documents** tab. The cards at the top summarize the collection:

| Card | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| Total documents | All documents in the collection, queued and indexed. |
| Query coverage | Percentage of documents that appeared in at least one search result among the recorded searches. A low value means much of the content is never retrieved. |
| Avg. Performance | Average processing time of a search, in milliseconds. |
| Avg. Score | Average score of the returned results, from 0 to 1. Higher is better. |

Low query coverage is not always a problem: a broad knowledge base can contain content that users rarely ask about. It deserves attention when documents you expect to be used never appear, which often points to documents that are too long, mixed-topic, or written differently from how users ask.

The document list below the cards shows each document's state, tags, reference, and token count, and can be filtered by state. Open **Details** on a document to see its timestamps, including when it was last indexed, and its character, word, and approximate token counts. The document editor warns when a document has too many or too few words for reliable retrieval; see [Write good documents](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md#write-good-documents).

## Search history

The **Transactions** tab lists the searches performed on the collection, including searches made by AI Gateways, MCP clients, and your applications. How long searches are kept depends on the plan; see [RAG search history retention](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#account-limits).

Use the **View** selector to choose what to review:

- **Recent** shows the newest searches.
- **Low quality** shows the lowest-scoring searches. Start here to find questions the collection answers poorly.
- **High quality** shows the highest-scoring searches.

Each search shows its moment, query, number of results, and three scores:

| Score | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Original score | Vector similarity between the query and the documents, before reranking. |
| Reranker score | Score assigned by the reranker, with the reranker name. A dash means no reranker was used. |
| Final score | Score used to rank the results. |

Open **Details** on a search to see its processing time, cost, scores, and the documents it returned, each with its original, reranker, and final score and a preview of the text. A document that was later deleted is shown as no longer existing.

### Diagnose a low-quality search

1. Read the query and compare it with the returned documents. If the right document is absent, the problem is retrieval, not ranking.
2. If the right document exists but scored low, check whether its text uses the same terms and language as the query, and whether it mixes several topics.
3. If the original score is good but the final score drops, compare rerankers; see [Rerankers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md).
4. If no document covers the question, add the missing knowledge to the collection.

For the pipeline stages that usually cause a low-quality result before the search runs, see [RAG vs vector database](https://aivax.net/blog/a-vector-database-is-not-a-rag-system/).

## Test searches in the playground

Select **Playground** on a collection to run a search without writing code. Set the search text, minimum score, maximum results, reranker, reference expansion, and [advanced filters](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md), then select **Run query**. The **Visual** tab shows the ranked documents with their scores, contents, and metadata, and the generated answer when you use answer generation; the **JSON** tab shows the raw result.

Use the playground to reproduce a low-quality search from the history, adjust options, and confirm an improvement before changing an AI Gateway. For processing time, cost, and per-stage scores, use the search details in **Transactions**.

## Media Injector jobs

Files imported with [Media Injector](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/documents.md#import-from-files-with-media-injector) are processed as background jobs. Follow them under **Batch > Media Processing**, which refreshes automatically and shows each job's collection, files, state, elapsed time, number of documents produced, current cost, and estimated cost. Cancel queued or processing jobs, and retry or delete failed or cancelled ones.

After a job completes, its documents appear in the collection as Queued until they are indexed.

## Cost and storage

- **Analytics > Usage per resource** groups usage by resource, including each collection, and links to it.
- **Analytics > Monthly Reports** shows the month's RAG cost, which includes embeddings, queries, and reranking.
- **Usage and limits** shows storage used against your plan quota.

De-duplication runs report their result through account notifications; see [De-duplicator](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md#de-duplicator).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.html

# Rerankers

Rerankers reorder an existing set of candidate documents for a query. They do not search a collection or recover text that is absent from the input. Use the autonomous reranking API when your application already owns the candidates, or use [Semantic Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md) to retrieve candidates from an AIVAX collection before reranking them.

[Reflex](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reflex.md) is the default ranker of this endpoint and AIVAX's collection-less search experience. See that page when you want retrieval-style ranking without managing a collection.

## Rerank documents directly

Authenticate with an [AIVAX API key](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/authentication.md) and send a query with the candidate document strings. The API returns the candidates in relevance order. Each result keeps its input position, so you can map it back to your application data.

Use direct reranking when candidates are dynamic, come from another search system, or do not need to be stored in an AIVAX collection. Use managed semantic search when AIVAX should retrieve candidates from a persistent corpus.

For the supported request, response, authentication, and error contract, use the API Reference:

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Rerank%20documents)

## Build candidates worth ranking

Reranking only reorders what it receives, so candidate quality decides the ceiling. Keep each candidate string focused on one idea — a paragraph or a short section rather than a whole page — so the relevance score reflects one topic instead of an average over many. When candidates come from chunking, prefer boundaries that preserve complete statements; see [Text segmentation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-processing/text-segmentation.md).

Use the [RAG pipeline checklist](https://aivax.net/blog/a-vector-database-is-not-a-rag-system/) to distinguish preparation, retrieval, and ordering failures.

Send enough candidates to cover plausible answers: over-retrieve first, then rank precisely. Use `top_n` to keep only the head of the ranked list, and `min_score` to drop low-relevance tail results. Calibrate that threshold on your own queries, because score scales differ between rankers and a cutoff tuned on one workload rarely transfers to another.

## Choosing a reranker

Start with the default reranker unless you have a measured reason to select another available option. The default is Reflex; alternatives include lexical matching, reciprocal-rank fusion of several signals, and third-party cross-encoders. Fusion (`rrf`) is retrieval-only and is rejected by this endpoint: it exists for combining signals inside collection search, not for autonomous ranking.

To compare options, fix a set of representative queries with known relevant documents from your own workload — covering your languages, document lengths, and jargon — and measure whether swapping rankers moves the right document upward. If the relevant document is missing from the candidates entirely, no ranker can recover it; improve candidate retrieval, chunking, query formulation, or candidate count before comparing rerankers.

To separate missing-candidate failures from poor-ordering failures before you add a reranker, see [Do I need a reranker for RAG?](https://aivax.net/blog/semantic-search-vs-reranking/). To judge when Reflex is enough, see [how Reflex compares with the other rerankers on this endpoint](https://aivax.net/blog/reflex-retrieval-built-for-recurring-documents/).

For current availability, supported options, and account limits, see the API Reference and [Plans and Limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reflex.html

# Reflex

Reflex is AIVAX's collection-less search for RAG. Send a query together with candidate document strings and receive the most relevant items in ranked order—without indexing, storing, or maintaining a RAG collection first.

Reflex is the default ranker of the autonomous [reranking endpoint](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/reranking.md): calling that endpoint without a `model` selects Reflex. This page explains when to choose Reflex; the reranking page covers candidate preparation and ranker comparison in depth.

Use Reflex when your application already owns the candidate documents, the candidate set changes frequently, or you want a retrieval step without collection indexing and storage. Use [Semantic Search](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/semantic-search.md) when AIVAX should store, index, and search a persistent knowledge base or narrow a corpus that is too large to submit as candidates on every request.

## Reflex or Semantic Search?

| Choose Reflex when... | Choose Semantic Search when... |
| --- | --- |
| Your application already has the candidate document strings. | Documents should live in managed AIVAX collections. |
| You need retrieval immediately, without an indexing step. | The knowledge base is persistent and searched repeatedly. |
| The candidate set is dynamic or request-specific. | The corpus is too large to submit as candidates on every request. |
| You want collection-less ranking. | You want collection filtering, stored metadata, document references, and managed retrieval. |

Reflex returns ranked text candidates; it does not generate an answer. Pass the selected documents to your language model or AI Gateway as RAG context. To decide between Reflex and a model reranker, see [best reranker for RAG](https://aivax.net/blog/reflex-retrieval-built-for-recurring-documents/).

## Use Reflex

Call the reranking API with a query and the candidate documents your application wants to compare. Results are returned in relevance order. Each result keeps its input position, so you can map it back to your application data.

Use concise, focused candidate documents. Reranking can improve their order, but it cannot recover information that was not included in the candidates. If the expected document is consistently absent, improve candidate selection, chunking, or query formulation before tuning the ranker.

Reflex limits the number of candidate documents per request and the number of ranked results returned; see [Pricing and limits](#pricing-and-limits). If your candidate pool exceeds the candidate limit, narrow it first — with lexical pre-filtering, a cheap first-pass rank, or collection retrieval — and let Reflex order the shortlist.

For the supported request, response, authentication, and error contract, use the API Reference:

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Rerank%20documents)

## Use Reflex with RAG

Reflex is also the default reranker after AIVAX retrieves candidates from RAG collections. In this flow, it can improve the order of retrieved candidates but cannot recover a document that the retrieval stage did not select. If relevant documents are consistently absent, adjust retrieval, chunking, query formulation, or candidate count before tuning reranking.

Every plan includes a daily reranking allowance for Reflex, shared between autonomous calls and RAG reranking. Cached and uncached input both consume this allowance. It is separate from the RAG embedding allowance and the processing-time cap; other rerankers are billed normally. For relative plan capacity and coverage rules, see [Plans and Limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#included-daily-subscription-allowances).

## Pricing and limits

Reflex is billed by input tokens. Input served from the account-scoped cache is billed at a lower rate. Accounts with [Data Sharing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/data-sharing.md) enabled receive a discount on eligible reranking operations.

| Description | Pricing |
| --- | ---: |
| Reflex - cache miss | **$0.015/M tokens** |
| Reflex - cache hit | **$0.003/M tokens** |

Each request accepts up to 10,000 candidate documents and returns up to 200 ranked results on every plan. Reflex processing time per day and reranking requests per minute depend on the plan; see [RAG and collections limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md#rag-and-collections).

The processing-time limit counts the time spent processing Reflex requests, both on the reranking endpoint and in RAG searches that use Reflex; cached input does not consume it separately. The reranking request limit applies to the reranking endpoint and to RAG searches that use a reranker, including searches through AI Gateways and MCP tools. Requests above a limit return `429 Too Many Requests`.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.html

# AI Gateway concepts

An AI Gateway stores a reusable inference configuration. Pass the gateway's ID or slug in the request's `model` field, and AIVAX applies its model settings, instructions, RAG collections, tools, skills, workers, moderation, and context controls before calling the model.

Use a gateway when the same behavior must be reused by multiple clients or changed without redeploying the calling application. Use a [direct inference call](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md) when the application controls the model, prompt, tools, and context of every request.

Treat the gateway configuration as sensitive: `GET /api/v1/ai-gateways/<id>` returns the full parameters to the owning account, including `apiKey` in plain text when the gateway uses an external provider key.

## Responsibility boundary

A gateway separates two roles:

- **The client application** sends messages and, with a private key, optional request overrides.
- **The gateway administrator** controls the operational policy: which model runs, what it is told, what it can read, which tools it can call, and which limits apply.

This boundary lets you change a model, a prompt, or a tool list in one place while every client keeps calling the same identifier. Each resource below is optional. Start with a model and system instructions, and add other resources only when the use case requires them: every tool, skill, or collection adds input tokens, cost, and one more path the model can choose wrongly.

The sections below describe what each resource does and when to use it. [Processing pipeline](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md) documents the detailed behavior of each step.

## Model and provider

The gateway's model is either an integrated AIVAX model or a model served by your own provider key (BYOK).

- **Integrated models** use `baseAddress: "@integrated"` and a model name such as `@openai/gpt-5-mini`. AIVAX selects the provider, bills the account, and applies [provider routing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md).
- **BYOK models** use the base address of an OpenAI-compatible provider endpoint, your provider `apiKey`, and the provider's model name. AIVAX still runs the gateway pipeline, but the provider bills you directly and provider routing does not apply. BYOK requests use the plan's BYOK rate limit; see [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md).

Use an integrated model unless you need a model, contract, or region that only your provider account offers. See [Models and gateway names](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/models-and-gateway-names.md) for how the model is identified.

## Model routing

Model routing selects a different model for each request. The complexity router classifies the latest user request as low, medium, or high complexity and runs the model configured for that level, with an optional reasoning effort per level. The response carries the `X-Model-Routed-Complexity` header when a level was selected.

Use it when most requests are simple but some need a stronger model, so you do not pay the stronger model's price on every request. Do not use it when every answer must come from the same model for consistency or compliance.

Model routing differs from [provider routing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md), which keeps the model and chooses which provider serves it.

## Instructions

Instruction settings shape the prompt the model receives:

| Resource | What it does | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| System instructions | Text added to the system instructions of every request. | Always. Describe the role, audience, sources of truth, and limits. |
| Remote instruction sources | URLs fetched as text and appended to the system instructions, with a configurable cache. | Instructions maintained in another system, such as a CMS or a repository, that must change without editing the gateway. |
| User prompt template | Replaces `{prompt}` with the text of each user message. | Every user message must be wrapped in the same frame, such as a fixed task description. |
| Assistant prefill | Initial assistant text placed before generation. | The answer must start with a fixed format. Some models do not support prefill. |

Write instructions about behavior, not about settings the gateway already controls, such as truncation limits or the tool list. See [Instructions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md#instructions) for the remote source size limit and failure rules.

## Model parameters

The gateway can set default values for `temperature`, `top_p`, `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`, `stop`, `max_completion_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`, and `verbosity`. `seed` is accepted only per request. Requests sent with a private key can override most of them; see [Override gateway values](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/using-an-ai-gateway.md#override-gateway-values).

Set parameters on the gateway when the behavior must be the same for every client, for example a low temperature for an extraction assistant. Some integrated models reject parameters such as temperature, stop sequences, or reasoning effort; AIVAX rejects the gateway configuration when the limitation is known.

## Context window and truncation

`contextMaximumSize` limits the approximate number of input tokens sent to the model, and `contextOverflowAction` decides what happens when a conversation exceeds it:

- `Throw` returns an error instead of calling the model. This is the default.
- `Truncate` removes the oldest non-system messages until the conversation fits, then continues.
- `TruncateHard` truncates like `Truncate`, but fails the request if the prompt still does not fit.

Use truncation for long-lived chats in which old turns lose relevance, such as support conversations. Keep `Throw` when every message matters, such as a document review, so the application decides what to remove. On the Free plan, the input context is capped regardless of this setting; see [Limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/limits.md). See [Context truncation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/context-truncation.md) for how messages are removed and when the check runs.

## Tool message truncation

`toolContextCount` keeps only the most recent tool results intact. Older tool messages stay in the conversation, but their content is replaced with a short note asking the model to call the tool again.

Use it in long agentic conversations whose tools return large payloads that are only relevant once, such as search results. Avoid it when an early tool result remains important later. Rewriting old messages also changes the request prefix, which can reduce [prompt caching](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/caching.md).

## Flags

Flags change how AIVAX prepares the provider request for models with specific behavior. Configure them in **Flags and normalization switches** in the gateway editor or in `parameters.flags`.

| Flag | Effect | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DisableMultiModalInput` | Images, audio, video, and files are not sent to the model, even when it supports them. | The gateway must stay text-only, for cost or policy reasons. |
| `ThinkingProcess` | Declares that the model reasons internally without returning its reasoning tokens. | A model that reasons but hides its reasoning. |
| `DiffusingStream` | Declares that the model is a diffusion model whose output is refined as a whole instead of produced token by token. | Diffusion models only. |
| `PreserveThinkingTokens` | Keeps the `<think>` blocks of earlier assistant messages in the conversation sent to the model. | Models that need their previous reasoning to continue a multi-step task. |
| `RewriteToolCallsAsUserMessages` | Rewrites tool calls and tool results as plain conversation messages. | Models or providers that reject the native tool message format. |
| `StrictUserAssistantTurns` | Enforces strict alternation between user and assistant messages. This disables tool messages. | Models that fail when two messages with the same role are adjacent. |
| `DisableReasoningSummary` | Stops streaming reasoning content to the client. | Clients that must never receive reasoning. |

Flags compensate for model limitations. Leave them unset unless you observe the problem a flag solves.

## Multimodal pre-processing

Multimodal pre-processing converts images, audio, video, and files into text before the main model runs. Each media type uses its own engine: a smaller or larger multimodal model, OCR, or speech-to-text.

Use it when the main model is text-only, or when a cheaper model can describe media once and a stronger text model can reason about the description. Do not use it when the main model must see the original media, such as when comparing visual details. See [Multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md) for the engines and their billing.

## Knowledge (RAG)

A gateway can link [collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md) so the model answers from your documents. The gateway controls the result limit, minimum score, reranker, reference behavior, and query strategy. Choose the strategy by conversation type:

- `Plain` searches with the last user message. Use it for standalone questions.
- `Concatenate` joins recent user messages. Use it when users split one question across several messages.
- `UserRewrite` and `FullRewrite` rewrite recent messages into search queries with a resolver model. Use them when follow-up questions depend on earlier turns, at the cost of an extra inference.
- `QueryFunction` gives the model a search tool so it decides when to search. Use it when many messages do not need retrieval. It requires a model with tool calling.

See [RAG](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md#rag) for the full behavior.

## Tools

Tools let the model act and read live data. A gateway can expose several kinds:

| Kind | Executed by | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md) | AIVAX | Common capabilities: date and time, web search, opening URLs, code, memory, and image, document, or page generation. |
| [MCP sources](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/mcp.md) | Your MCP server, called by AIVAX | You already have an MCP server or a catalog of business tools shared by several agents. |
| [Protocol functions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/protocol-functions.md) | Your HTTP callback, called by AIVAX | One or a few specific actions, without running a full MCP server. |
| [Shell](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/shell.md) | An AIVAX sandbox | Tasks easier to express as commands, or many tools moved behind a command line. |
| Raw `tools` | Your client application | The client must execute the action itself; see [Tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/tools.md). |

Built-in tools, MCP tools, protocol functions, and the shell are server-side tools: AIVAX runs them during the request and returns only the final answer. Enable only tools with a clear role, and give them specific names and restrictive schemas.

## Skills

[Skills](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/skills.md) are instruction packs the model loads on demand. Use them for specialized procedures that only some requests need, so their text does not occupy the system instructions of every request.

## Tool handler

The tool handler, or function interpreter, is deprecated. It adds tool calling for models that do not produce reliable native tool calls: `native` or no value uses the model's native tool calling; `react.v1.selfcall` uses a ReAct-style handler.

Do not use it in new gateways; choose a model with native tool calling instead. See [Function interpreter (deprecated)](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/function-interpreter.md).

## Tool explanations

`toolInvocationExplanations` asks the model to explain each server-side tool call with a short reason and goal, which AIVAX returns with the tool event. Use it when the client shows tool activity to end users. See [Tool explanations](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/response-rendering/tool-explanations.md).

## Moderation

Input moderation evaluates the textual conversation before the main model runs and makes the model refuse requests that reach the configured sensitivity in a category. Use it for broad safety policy in user-facing assistants. It does not moderate output or media, and it is not an authorization mechanism. See [Moderation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/moderation.md).

## Workers

[Workers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md) call your endpoint during gateway events, so your code can block a message, rewrite context, add tools, or replace a tool result. Use them when a decision depends on data only your system has, such as the user's account state. The worker runs in the critical path, so keep it fast and deterministic.

## Time zone

`timeZone` sets the IANA time zone the model uses to read and write dates. It applies to `get_date_time`, scheduling tools, and the shell, and defaults to `America/Sao_Paulo`. Set it to your users' time zone; a request can override it with `time_zone`.

## Pricing

A gateway has no separate fee. Requests are billed by the model and the resources the gateway uses: inference tokens, rewrite or pre-processing inferences, moderation, tools, and RAG. See [Inference pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md#pricing).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/models-and-gateway-names.html

# Models and gateway names

The `model` field of `/v1/chat/completions` selects what runs the request. It accepts three kinds of value:

| Value | Example | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Integrated model name | `@openai/gpt-5-mini` | The model directly, with no gateway configuration. |
| Gateway full ID | `<GATEWAY_UUID>` | The AI Gateway with that ID. |
| Gateway slug | `support:50c3` | The AI Gateway whose slug matches, in the format `name:final-id`. |

Integrated model names start with `@` and follow `@creator/model-name`. List them with `GET /v1/models`; the same list includes the gateways of your account.

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Model%20listing)

Public API keys accept only a gateway's full ID. Slugs and integrated model names are rejected; see [Authentication](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/authentication.md).

An integrated model name can carry a provider routing suffix, such as `@openai/gpt-6-luna#cheapest`. See [Inline routing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/inline-routing.md).

## Choose a model for a gateway

Validate three points before putting a model into production:

- The model supports the input modalities you intend to send, such as image, audio, video, or file. Otherwise, enable [multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md).
- The model supports function calling if the gateway uses tools, `QueryFunction` RAG, MCP, protocol functions, skills, or built-in tools.
- The model accepts the parameters you configure. Some integrated models reject assistant prefill, temperature, stop sequences, or reasoning effort.

## Replace a model

A gateway lets you change the model behind a stable name, so client applications do not change when a model is retired. You still need to qualify the replacement with your own prompts and tools before switching. To tell a current model from an old one, see [Deprecated models](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md#deprecated-models).

See [pinning a model ID versus using an alias](https://aivax.net/blog/pin-llm-model-id-or-use-alias-model-deprecations/) for a replacement checklist. For the GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 shutdown on January 14, 2027, see [how to migrate to gpt-6-luna](https://aivax.net/blog/migrate-gpt-4o-and-gpt-4-1-to-gpt-6-luna/). For the GPT-5 and o3 shutdown on December 11, 2026, see [how to migrate to GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna](https://aivax.net/blog/migrate-gpt-5-and-o3-to-gpt-5-6-before-december-11/).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/using-an-ai-gateway.html

# Using an AI Gateway

Create a gateway in the dashboard or with the API, then call it through the OpenAI-compatible `chat/completions` endpoint by passing its ID or slug as `model`.

## Create and manage gateways

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Create%20AI%20Gateway)

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Edit%20AI%20Gateway)

An edit request may contain only the fields to change; omitted fields keep their current values.

## Call the gateway

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Inference%20(chat%20completions))

```json
{
    "model": "support:50c3",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "How do I reset my password?"
        }
    ]
}
```

The request carries only the conversation. The gateway adds its instructions, retrieved documents, and tools before the model runs. To understand how this pre-configuration changes the request, see [Inference with AI Gateways](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/ai-gateways.md).

## Override gateway values

Requests sent with a private key can override supported gateway values for that request only. The gateway itself is not changed.

| Request field | Overrides |
| --- | --- |
| `temperature`, `top_p`, `seed`, `presence_penalty` | Sampling parameters. |
| `reasoning_effort`, `verbosity` | Reasoning and verbosity settings, when the model supports them. |
| `max_completion_tokens`, `stop` | Output length and stop sequences. |
| `tools` | Adds client-side tools to the gateway tools. |
| `builtin_tools` | Enables additional [built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/built-in-tools.md). |
| `response_schema`, `response_format` | [Structured output](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/structured-output.md). |
| `time_zone` | The gateway time zone. |
| `multimodal_resolver` | The [multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md) engines. |
| `tool_invocation_explanations` | [Tool explanations](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/response-rendering/tool-explanations.md). |
| `routing_options` | [Provider routing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md#override-routing-per-request). |

`frequency_penalty` is configured only on the gateway. Instructions, RAG, MCP sources, protocol functions, skills, workers, and moderation cannot be overridden per request.

Public API keys accept only a small set of request fields and reject the others; see [Limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/limits.md#public-api-keys).

## Test incrementally

When a gateway behaves unexpectedly, test a plain prompt first, then add RAG, tools, media, or structured output one at a time. This isolates the resource that causes the problem. See [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/troubleshooting.md).

## Use a gateway from MCP clients

To expose an integrated model or an AI Gateway as a tool for an external MCP client, see [Inference MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/mcp-utilities/inference-mcp.md).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/using-sdks.html

# Using AI Gateways via SDKs

The inference endpoint follows the OpenAI chat completions shape, so existing OpenAI-compatible SDKs work by changing the base URL and the API key. Load your private API key from secure configuration; see [Make your first request](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.md#make-your-first-request) for an environment-variable example.

```python {title="gateway.py"}
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://inference.aivax.net/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["AIVAX_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="my-gateway:50c3",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain why AI gateways are useful."}
    ],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

```js {title="gateway.js"}
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
    baseURL: "https://inference.aivax.net/v1",
    apiKey: process.env.AIVAX_API_KEY,
});

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
    model: "my-gateway:50c3",
    messages: [
        { role: "user", content: "Explain why AI gateways are useful." }
    ],
});

console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

Replace `my-gateway:50c3` with your gateway's full ID or slug.

OpenAI-compatible inference uses `/v1/chat/completions`. The `/v1/responses` endpoint is not supported.

## Send AIVAX fields

AIVAX extensions, such as `conversation_token`, `builtin_tools`, `response_schema`, `routing_options`, or `metadata`, are not part of the SDK's typed parameters. Send them as extra request-body fields:

```python
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="my-gateway:50c3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What changed in my order?"}],
    extra_body={
        "conversation_token": "order-thread-1042",
        "metadata": {"workflow": "order-support"},
    },
)
```

In the JavaScript SDK, add the fields directly to the request object; the SDK sends them in the request body. In TypeScript, the extra fields may need a type cast.

> [!NOTE]
> The Python SDK's `extra_body` argument only adds fields to the request body. It is different from the AIVAX `extra_body` request field, which forwards custom JSON to a BYOK provider; see [Custom JSON](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/custom-json.md).

Fields that AIVAX adds to responses, such as `conversation_token`, `provider`, or `generation_context`, are available through the SDK's raw response or the untyped properties of the returned object.

## Long requests

Requests with long reasoning or many tool calls can exceed the proxy timeout of the default host. Use the direct inference host `https://direct.inference.aivax.net/v1` as `base_url` and raise the SDK timeout; see [Long-running inference](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.md#long-running-inference).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/going-to-production.html

# Taking an AI Gateway to production

Start with a conservative configuration: clear system instructions, a model that supports the required modalities and tools, one well-prepared RAG collection, and only the tools that are actually needed. Add resources one at a time and measure their effect on quality, cost, and latency.

## System instructions

Write the system instructions so the model understands its role, audience, sources of truth, and limits. Include when to use RAG, when to use tools, and how to respond when information is unavailable. Avoid repeating operational settings that already exist in the gateway, such as truncation limits or tool lists.

If your prompts currently live in OpenAI Prompt Objects or Agent Builder, see [what you lose when they shut down and where each piece can live](https://aivax.net/blog/openai-prompt-objects-agent-builder-shutdown-what-you-lose/).

## Knowledge

Link collections with short, self-contained, well-named documents, and choose the query strategy by conversation type; see [Knowledge (RAG)](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md#knowledge-rag). Start with a small result count and raise it only when the model lacks evidence, because each result adds input tokens.

## Tools

Enable only tools with a clear role. Built-in tools cover common capabilities. External MCP is better when you already have an MCP server with business tools. Protocol functions are useful when you want to expose specific HTTP callbacks without installing a full MCP server. Every tool adds its name, description, and schema to each request; see [how to measure and cut tool-definition tokens](https://aivax.net/blog/reduce-mcp-tool-definition-tokens-too-many-tools/).

Use a tool handler only when the selected model needs help producing tool calls.

## Memory

When enabling [memory](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md#memory), define what the assistant may retain and when it must call `memory_search`: memories are not automatically included in system instructions. By default, memories are shared across the account's gateways for the same identified user; disable shared memory to restrict a gateway to its own memories. Memories only expire when saved with `expiresInDays`. Plan how your application will review and remove documents in the `@memories` collection. The [memory-poisoning guide](https://aivax.net/blog/persistent-memory-is-a-write-path/) outlines these controls.

## Workers and moderation

Use workers when an external system must decide something during the inference flow. Because the worker is called in the critical path, keep it fast and deterministic.

When you enable moderation, see [LLM input moderation: system prompt or separate moderation step?](https://aivax.net/blog/aivax-gateway-moderation/) for what it covers, its failure behavior, and what still needs application-level checks.

## Client integration

- Keep private keys on the server. Use a public key or a [chat client](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md) for code that runs in a browser.
- Send one [`conversation_token`](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/session-reuse.md) per conversation and store the message IDs AIVAX returns.
- Configure retries for `429` and `503` responses; see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/troubleshooting.md).
- Use [streaming](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/streaming.md) for user-facing chats, or the direct inference host for long non-streaming requests.

## Validate before release

Validate the configuration with a [simulated-user and LLM-judge scenario](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/agentic-tests.md) before relying on it in production, and run the same scenarios again after changing the model, instructions, or tools.

Review [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md) and [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md) before increasing traffic.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.html

# Inference concepts

AIVAX exposes an OpenAI-compatible `chat/completions` API with additional AIVAX parameters. The additions are optional and are designed to support gateways, RAG, built-in tools, structured responses, multimodal pre-processing, provider routing, and billing metadata.

These pages cover the request contract. Use an [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md) when the same configuration must be reused or centrally managed.

## Direct call or gateway

Use a direct call for simple tasks, tests, internal routines, and integrations where the application controls the model, prompt, tools, and context for each request.

Use an AI Gateway when behavior needs to be stable, auditable, and reusable. Gateways are better for support assistants, chat bots, RAG agents, permanent tools, workers, skills, and configurations shared by multiple clients.
