See [Inference with AI Gateways](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/ai-gateways.md) for how a gateway changes a request.

## How a request runs

One request can involve several model generations. AIVAX prepares the context, calls the model, runs any server-side tools the model requests, calls the model again with their results, and repeats until the model produces a final answer or requests a tool your client must run.

1. **Prepare.** AIVAX resolves the model or gateway, adds gateway instructions and retrieved documents, restores [server-side context](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/server-side-context.md) from earlier turns, applies [pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md) and moderation, and fits the conversation to the context window.
2. **Generate.** The selected provider generates reasoning, text, or tool calls; see [Routing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md) for how the provider is chosen.
3. **Run server-side tools.** [Built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/built-in-tools.md), [MCP tools, and protocol functions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/mcp-and-protocol-functions.md) run inside AIVAX, and the loop returns to step 2.
4. **Finish.** AIVAX validates [structured output](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/structured-output.md) when requested, and returns the final answer, or the [client tool calls](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/tools.md) your application must run.

Only the final result is returned as an assistant message. With [streaming](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/streaming.md), you also receive reasoning, tool events, and partial text as they happen.

## Endpoint

<div class="request-item post">
    <span>POST</span>
    <span>
        /v1/chat/completions
    </span>
</div>

The endpoint also has the API alias `/api/v1/chat/completions`.

Reference:

[API endpoint reference](https://inference.aivax.net/apidocs?embed=iframe&embed-endpoint=Inference%20(chat%20completions))

## Long-running inference

Because one request can run several generations and tools, it can take minutes. On `https://inference.aivax.net`, a non-streaming request that exceeds the proxy timeout ends with HTTP `524` while AIVAX keeps processing it. Send long requests to the direct inference host instead:

```text
https://direct.inference.aivax.net/v1
```

The request is still synchronous: keep the connection open and set a client timeout that covers the expected processing time. Paths, keys, and request bodies are the same as on the default host. Streaming requests send data continuously and rarely need it. See [Long-running inference](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/overview.md#long-running-inference) for an SDK example and the endpoints the direct host serves.

## Request metadata

Set `metadata` to attach string key/value information to the inference request. AIVAX stores this object with the logged conversation and exposes it to gateway events, so it is useful for operational correlation such as an order ID, tenant, workflow, or internal trace key.

```json
{
    "model": "your-model-or-gateway-id",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Summarize this support ticket."
        }
    ],
    "metadata": {
        "ticket_id": "SUP-1042",
        "workflow": "support-triage"
    }
}
```

`metadata` must be a JSON object whose property names and values are strings. Do not place secrets, credentials, payment data, or large payloads in this field.

## Response and conversation records

The standard `/v1/chat/completions` response envelope includes `generation_context`. Its `generated_usage` entries contain `sku`, `amount`, `unit_price`, `quantity`, and `description`. Set [`json_only: true`](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/structured-responses/json-only.md) to return only the final JSON without this envelope.

`usage` reports `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, and `total_tokens`. `prompt_tokens` counts only uncached input; cached input is reported separately in `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. See [Caching](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/caching.md).

Responses for integrated models also include `provider`, the tag of the provider that served the request; see [Provider in responses](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md#provider-in-responses).

Set `allow_logging: false` in a `/v1/chat/completions` request to keep that request out of the account conversation logs. It defaults to `true`, and it cannot enable logging when conversation logging is disabled for the account. Usage and billing records are still created.

When conversation logging is enabled, the stored record includes its ID, origin, model name, request ID, response schema, tools and tool input schemas, usage, linked resources, created and updated timestamps, token count, external user ID, error message, messages, and metadata. Gateway and API key context is available through the linked resources.

Use `conversation_token` and `metadata` to correlate these records with your own workflow.

## Pricing

Inference rates depend on the selected model, provider, input size, and media type. Moderation is charged separately in Processing Units (PUs), covering input, cached input, and output usage; its PU price varies with the model and provider used. The [plan multiplier](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md#plan-multipliers) applies to integrated-model inference and moderation. BYOK is not affected by it. In usage records, moderation charges appear under the model `@aivax/layered-moderation`.

| Description | Pricing |
| --- | ---: |
| AI model and AI Gateway inference | Selected model and provider rates |
| Input moderation | Variable price per PU; separate from the main inference charge |

One moderation PU equals one output token of the moderation model, and input tokens count in proportion to their price. For example, with a model priced at $0.10/M input and $0.40/M output tokens, a check using 3,000 input and 50 output tokens consumes 800 PUs (3,000 × 0.25 + 50), about $0.00032 before the plan multiplier.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/server-side-context.html

# Server-side context

`chat/completions` is stateless: each request carries the conversation it needs, and AIVAX does not keep a message history for you. Some of the context the model works with, however, is created or added on the server and never appears in the messages you send or receive. This page explains what that context is, so you can predict what the model sees.

## What AIVAX adds before the model runs

Before each generation, AIVAX can add context that your request did not contain:

| Context | Source | Returned to you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| System instructions and remote instruction sources | [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md#instructions) | No |
| Retrieved documents | Gateway [RAG](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md#rag) collections | No, unless the model quotes them |
| Skill instructions | [Skills](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/skills.md) the model loads | No |
| Tool definitions | Gateway tools, MCP sources, protocol functions, `builtin_tools` | No |
| Descriptions of media | [Multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md) | No |
| Context added by a worker | [Workers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md) | No |

This context is rebuilt on every request from the current gateway configuration. Changing the gateway changes the next request; it does not rewrite earlier answers.

## What AIVAX creates during the request

When the model calls a [server-side tool](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/mcp-and-protocol-functions.md), AIVAX runs it and adds the call and its result to the conversation before generating again. A single request can contain many of these steps. The response returns only the final assistant message, with the text of every step joined together; the tool calls and their results are not returned as messages.

With streaming, you can observe these steps as they happen through `servertool` events and reasoning, but they are still not part of the final `messages` you would send back. See [Streaming](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/streaming.md).

## Keep the context across turns

Because tool calls and results are not returned, the history you send on the next turn lacks them. Without them, the model can lose data it already obtained and call the same tools again.

Send the same `conversation_token` on every request of the conversation, and AIVAX restores those tool calls and results into the history before the model runs. The restored state expires one hour after its last use. See [Session reuse](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/session-reuse.md) for the token rules and how AIVAX matches stored turns.

Client-side tools are different: their calls are returned to you, and your application sends their results back as `tool` messages, so they are always part of the history you control. See [Tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/tools.md).

## What is not kept

- **The message history.** Your application stores it and sends it on every request. If AIVAX should store it, use a [chat client session](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md).
- **Reasoning.** Session reuse restores tool calls and results, not reasoning. Send back the final assistant answer, not the reasoning transcript; see [Raw multi-turn example](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/response-rendering/raw-multi-turn-example.md).
- **Long-term memory.** Facts the assistant should remember across conversations require the [memory tool](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md#memory).

## Conversation records

When conversation logging is enabled, AIVAX stores a record of the conversation for observability, and requests with the same `conversation_token` update the same record. This record is for inspection and auditing; it is not used as context for later requests. See [Response and conversation records](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md#response-and-conversation-records).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/session-reuse.html

# Session reuse

Session reuse lets a stateless `chat/completions` client keep the server-side context of a conversation between requests. Your application still stores and sends the message history; AIVAX only restores what the history cannot carry. For what that context contains, see [Server-side context](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/server-side-context.md).

## Session reuse and chat client sessions

AIVAX has two features with "session" in the name. They solve different problems:

| | Session reuse (`conversation_token`) | [Chat client session](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who stores the message history | Your application. It sends the full history on every request. | AIVAX. The client sends only the new message. |
| What AIVAX keeps | Server-side tool calls and results of recent turns, for one hour after last use. | The whole conversation, context, metadata, and limits, until the session expires. |
| Endpoint | `/v1/chat/completions` | Chat client session endpoints, the web widget, and messaging integrations. |
| Identity | An opaque token you choose or AIVAX returns. | A session access key, optionally tied to a stable user `tag`. |
| Best for | Backends, agents, and SDK integrations that already manage conversations. | End-user chats in browsers, WhatsApp, or Telegram, where AIVAX manages the conversation. |

A chat client session manages its own conversation token internally; you do not send `conversation_token` to it. Use session reuse when your application owns the history, and a chat client when AIVAX should own it.

## Send the token

Send `conversation_token` in every request of the same conversation. AIVAX uses it to restore what happened on the server side in earlier turns, and to update a single stored conversation record instead of creating a new one for each request.

Server-side tools, such as [built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md), MCP tools, and protocol functions, run inside AIVAX. Their calls and results are not returned to you as messages: the response contains only the final assistant message, with the text of every step joined together. When you send the conversation history back, those tool calls and results are missing. With the same `conversation_token`, AIVAX puts them back into the history before the model runs, so the model still sees the data its tools returned and does not repeat the same calls.

```json
{
    "model": "your-model-or-gateway-id",
    "conversation_token": "support-ticket-1042",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "What is the status of order 123?"
        },
        {
            "id": "aivx_k2m9x0q4tr",
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": "Order 123 was shipped yesterday and should arrive on Friday."
        },
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Can you change the delivery address?"
        }
    ]
}
```

You can create the token yourself and send it from the first request of the conversation; you do not need to wait for AIVAX to return one. Any non-empty string with 128 characters or less is accepted, with no required format, such as the ID your application already uses for the conversation. Tokens are scoped to your account, so another account can use the same value without sharing state with yours. When omitted, AIVAX generates a token and returns it, and you can reuse the returned value from the second request on.

Every response returns two values:

| Field | Where | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conversation_token` | Response root. When streaming, the last chunk before `[DONE]`. | Send it in the next request of the conversation. |
| Message ID (`aivx_...`) | The response `id` and `choices[].message.id`. When streaming, the `id` of every chunk, including tool and error chunks. | Recommended. Store it with the assistant message and send it back as that message's `id`. |

AIVAX matches the assistant messages you send back with its stored turns in this order:

1. The `id` of the assistant message, when you send it.
2. The IDs of the tool calls it carries, when the turn also requested tools from your client.
3. The text of the message, within the same `conversation_token`.

Matching by `id` is the most reliable. Matching by text is a fallback for clients that discard the `id`, and it can fail without an error, for example when the text was changed or when two answers in the same conversation have the same text. When no match is found, the message is used exactly as you sent it.

## Client requirements

- **Use one token per conversation.** Reusing a token across different conversations, users, or branches can restore tool results from another conversation. Generate a new token when a new conversation starts, and do not use values that users can guess or choose.
- **Do not share tokens between end users.** The token is not a credential, but anyone who can call your account with it can continue that conversation's stored context.
- **Store and resend the message `id`.** Save the `aivx_...` ID of every assistant message you receive and send it back as the `id` of that message in later requests. This is the recommended way to restore a turn, and it keeps working when the text alone cannot identify it.
- **Send back the exact content AIVAX returned.** Keep the full text of each assistant message as you received it, including the text the model wrote before calling tools, joined in a single assistant message. Do not split it into several messages, drop parts of it, or rewrite, translate, or summarize it. Matching by text ignores whitespace only. When `rendering_mode` is `textual_blocks`, the content mixes reasoning and answer blocks, so only the `id` can identify the turn.
- **Preserve tool call IDs.** When a response requests tools from your client, send back the same `tool_calls[].id` values and answer each one with a `tool` message.
- **Handle expired state.** The server-side state of a turn expires after one hour without use. After that, or when it cannot be found, the conversation continues normally, but the model no longer sees the results of those earlier server-side tools.
- **Do not resend restored tools yourself.** You do not need to rebuild server-side tool calls or results. If your history already contains them with the same IDs, AIVAX does not add them again.

`idempotency_key` is a deprecated alias of `conversation_token`. It still works, but new integrations should use `conversation_token`. When both are sent, they must have the same value; otherwise the request fails with `400 Bad Request`.

To keep conversation state in your application and gateway configuration in AIVAX, see [migrating Assistants threads to Responses](https://aivax.net/blog/migrating-from-openai-assistants-without-rebuilding-the-same-coupling/).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/ai-gateways.html

# Inference with AI Gateways

An AI Gateway pre-configures an inference. When `model` is a gateway ID or slug, the request you send is only part of the request the model receives: AIVAX merges it with the gateway configuration first.

```json
{
    "model": "support:50c3",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Where is my order 123?"
        }
    ]
}
```

With a gateway configured with instructions, a collection, and a protocol function, the model receives the gateway's system instructions, the documents retrieved for the question, and the function definition, in addition to the user message. The same request sent with `"model": "@openai/gpt-5-mini"` would reach the model with only the user message.

## What the gateway sets

| Area | Set by the gateway | Can the request change it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model and provider | Model, BYOK endpoint, model routing, provider routing | Provider routing, with [`routing_options`](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md#override-routing-per-request) |
| Instructions | System instructions, remote sources, prompt template, prefill | No. The request can add its own `system` messages. |
| Parameters | Temperature, top-p, penalties, stop, output limit, reasoning effort, verbosity, seed | Yes, except `frequency_penalty` |
| Knowledge | Collections, query strategy, result limits, reranker | No |
| Tools | Built-in tools, MCP sources, protocol functions, skills, shell, raw tools | The request can add `tools` and `builtin_tools`, but cannot remove gateway tools. |
| Media | Multimodal pre-processing engines, `DisableMultiModalInput` | Engines, with `multimodal_resolver` |
| Context | Context window, overflow action, tool message truncation | No |
| Policy | Moderation, workers | No |
| Presentation | Tool explanations, time zone | Yes |

The full list of request overrides is in [Override gateway values](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/using-an-ai-gateway.md#override-gateway-values). Values in the request apply to that request only and never change the gateway.

## Precedence

When the same setting comes from several places, the most specific one wins:

1. The request field, such as `temperature` or `routing_options`.
2. A suffix in the gateway's model name, for routing; see [Inline routing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/inline-routing.md).
3. The gateway configuration.
4. The model's defaults.

Account settings, such as [ZDR](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/zdr.md) or [special providers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/special-providers.md), restrict the result regardless of these values.

## Public keys

Public API keys can call only gateways, by full ID, and accept a reduced set of request fields. With a public key, the gateway's MCP sources, protocol functions, built-in tools, shell, and skills are not used, so the gateway configuration is the only place where its behavior is defined. See [Limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/limits.md#public-api-keys).

## When to move settings into a gateway

Move a setting from the request into a gateway when every client sends the same value, when non-developers need to change it, or when it must not be controlled by the client, such as instructions, tools, or moderation. Keep it in the request when it varies per call, such as `metadata`, `conversation_token`, or a per-task `response_schema`.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.html

# Processing pipeline

When a request uses an [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md), AIVAX runs a fixed sequence of steps before, during, and after each model generation. Each step can add context, change the conversation, expose tools, or stop the request. Knowing the order helps you predict what each step can see: for example, moderation sees the documents retrieved by RAG, but not the descriptions produced by multimodal pre-processing.

Most steps are configured in the gateway parameters. Requests sent with a private key can override some of them; see [Inference with AI Gateways](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/ai-gateways.md).

## Order of execution

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Request received] --> B[Prepare: skills and RAG retrieval]
    B --> C[Resolve model, provider, tools and instructions]
    C --> D[Apply request overrides]
    D --> E[Worker: message.received]
    E --> F[Restore server-side context]
    F --> G[Moderation]
    G --> H[Build system instructions]
    H --> I[Context window check and truncation]
    I --> J[Multimodal pre-processing]
    J --> K[Tool message truncation, prompt template, prefill]
    K --> L[Assemble tools]
    L --> M[Model generation]
    M -->|server-side tool calls| N[Worker: tool.called, then run tools]
    N --> H
    M -->|final answer or client tool calls| O[Structured output, usage and conversation record]
```

Steps 1 to 6 run once per request. Steps 7 to 12 form the agentic loop and run again every time the model calls a server-side tool.

| # | Step | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Prepare](#rag) | Once | Loads the gateway skills. For injection query strategies, searches the linked collections and inserts the results into the last user message. Collection contexts are added to the system instructions. |
| 2 | Resolve | Once | Resolves the model and provider through [routing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/routing/setup-routing.md), fetches [remote instruction sources](#instructions), loads protocol functions, protocol function sources, MCP tools, and gateway built-in tools, and applies the gateway [parameters](#parameterization). |
| 3 | Request overrides | Once | Applies request fields such as `temperature`, `tools`, `builtin_tools`, `multimodal_resolver`, and `response_format`. |
| 4 | [Worker `message.received`](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md#messagereceived) | Once | Calls your worker, which can stop the request or change messages, instructions, tools, and MCP sources. |
| 5 | Server-side context | Once | Restores the [server-side context](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/server-side-context.md) of earlier turns when [session reuse](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/session-reuse.md) applies, and removes orphaned tool messages. |
| 6 | [Moderation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/moderation.md) | Once | Evaluates the conversation text and blocks it, or adds self-assessment instructions and the refusal tool. |
| 7 | System instructions | Each iteration | Joins gateway instructions, remote sources, collection contexts, the `system` messages of the request, the skill list, and tool explanation guidance. |
| 8 | [Context truncation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/context-truncation.md) | Each iteration | Compares the approximate input size with `contextMaximumSize` and applies `contextOverflowAction`. |
| 9 | [Multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md) | Each iteration | Replaces media with textual descriptions using the configured engines. Results are cached, so media is described only once. |
| 10 | Message rewriting | Each iteration | Applies [tool message truncation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/context-truncation.md#tool-message-truncation), the [user prompt template](#instructions), and, on the first iteration only, the [assistant prefill](#instructions). |
| 11 | Tool assembly | Each iteration | Joins request tools and server-side tools, removes identical duplicates, and rejects the request when two different tools share a name. With a [function interpreter](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/function-interpreter.md), tool selection happens here instead of in the provider call. |
| 12 | Generation and tools | Each iteration | Calls the provider. Server-side tool calls go through the [worker `tool.called` event](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md#toolcalled), run inside AIVAX, go through the [worker `tool.fetched` event](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md#toolfetched), and return to step 7 with their results. |
| 13 | Finalization | Once | Validates or heals [structured output](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/structured-output.md), records usage and cost, stores the conversation when logging is enabled, and notifies the [worker `message.completed` event](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md#messagecompleted) without waiting for it. |

### What the order means in practice

- **Workers run before moderation.** A worker can block a request without spending moderation, and moderation evaluates the conversation after the worker changed it.
- **Moderation sees retrieved documents.** RAG results are inserted into the last user message before moderation runs, so the safeguard evaluates them together with the user's text.
- **Moderation does not see media.** Multimodal pre-processing runs after moderation, so media descriptions are not moderated.
- **Moderation runs once per request.** Tool results produced during the agentic loop are not moderated.
- **Truncation can happen in the middle of a request.** The context check runs on every iteration, so large tool results can cause older messages to be removed, or a `Throw` error, after some tools already ran.
- **The context size is measured before pre-processing.** Media is counted by its original size estimate, not by the size of its textual description.
- **The prompt template applies to every user message,** including messages that carry retrieved RAG documents.

## RAG

The RAG step adds knowledge from your documents to the model context. It links [collections](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md) to an AI Gateway. The gateway controls:

- Collections included in retrieval.
- Maximum number of retrieved documents.
- Minimum score.
- Reranker name.
- Whether chunk references are included.
- Query strategy.

When a gateway has knowledge collections and the latest user message contains text, AIVAX can retrieve matching documents before the model call. For injection strategies, the retrieved context is inserted at the beginning of the last user message. If a linked collection has its own context text, that collection context is added to system instructions.

Query strategies:

- `Plain`: Uses the latest user message as the search query.
- `Concatenate`: Joins the latest configured number of user messages line by line and searches with the combined text.
- `UserRewrite`: Rewrites recent user messages into one or more search queries using a resolver model.
- `FullRewrite`: Rewrites recent user and assistant messages into one or more search queries using a resolver model.
- `QueryFunction`: Adds a query function to the model. The model decides when to search the linked collections, and search results are returned as tool responses. The model can narrow a search with an optional [document filter](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/document-filters.md).

Rewrite strategies add resolver-model cost (see [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md)) and latency. They are useful when follow-up questions depend on earlier turns.

Defining many RAG results increases input token usage and can increase final inference cost (see [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md)). Start with a small result count and raise it only when the model lacks enough evidence.

## Instructions

Instruction settings shape the provider-facing prompt:

- **System instructions**: Added to the system instruction set.
- **Remote system instruction sources**: Fetched from configured URLs and added to the system instruction set.
- **User prompt template**: Replaces `{prompt}` with each user message's text before sending it to the model. The templated message is sent as text only, so media attached to user messages is not sent to the model when a template is set.
- **Assistant prefill**: Adds initial assistant content before generation when the model supports prefill.

Remote instruction sources are fetched as text, and each response has a size limit; see [Inference limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/limits.md#remote-instruction-sources). Their cache duration is configurable from 0 (no caching) to 86,400 seconds; the default is 600 seconds.

If a source cannot be read (response over the limit, failed request, or unsafe URL), it contributes no text and the request itself does not fail. Keep these failure rules in mind:

- A failed fetch (an HTTP error such as 404 or 500, a connection error, a private URL, or a response over the limit) contributes no text and is cached for at most 30 seconds, or for the configured duration when it is shorter.
- There is no stale-if-error fallback. If a previously good source expires during an outage, the model receives only the `# <name>` title with no body (or nothing, if the source has no name).
- No error or log entry is shown when this happens.

Some models do not support assistant prefill, temperature, stop sequences, or reasoning effort. Integrated model validation rejects incompatible gateway settings when those limitations are known.

## Skills

Skills are on-demand instruction packs available to the model. Use them for specialized instructions that only some tasks need. When a gateway enables skills, AIVAX loads the account skills configured on the gateway and can expose skill-related built-in functions.

Read more about [skills](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/skills.md).

## Multimodal pre-processing

Multimodal pre-processing converts selected media content into text before the main model call. Each content type (images, audio, video, and files) uses its own engine: a smaller (`InferenceLow`) or larger (`InferenceHigh`) multimodal model, OCR for images and files, or speech-to-text for audio. See [Multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md) for the accepted engines.

The gateway setting `multimodalResolverParameters` replaces the deprecated `enabledMultimodalFeatures` flags. Gateways that still use the flags keep working with the equivalent engines until `multimodalResolverParameters` is set.

Use pre-processing when the main model is text-first or when you want AIVAX to normalize media into textual context. For direct multimodal models, send the original media without pre-processing so the model can inspect it directly.

Results are cached by content and engine for reuse.

## Parameterization

The gateway sets default model request options, such as:

- `temperature`
- `top_p`
- `presence_penalty`
- `frequency_penalty`
- `stop`
- `max_completion_tokens`
- `reasoning_effort`
- `verbosity`

Request-level values can override gateway values when the endpoint supports the parameter. `seed` is accepted only per request. `frequency_penalty` is configured only on the gateway and is not overridden per request. Some integrated models reject specific parameters, and BYOK providers may have their own restrictions.

## Context truncation

`contextMaximumSize`, `contextOverflowAction`, and `toolContextCount` keep long conversations within a maximum input size. See [Context truncation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/context-truncation.md).

## Moderation

Input moderation blocks unsafe or out-of-policy requests before the main model answers them. See [Moderation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/moderation.md).

## Server-side tools

Server-side tools are internal functions executed by AIVAX during inference. They can come from:

- Built-in tools.
- Protocol functions.
- Remote protocol function sources.
- MCP sources.
- QueryFunction RAG.
- Skills.
- Optional bash environment.

Server-side tool events can be streamed to clients as `servertool` updates.

## Built-in tools

Built-in tools can be configured on a gateway or supplied per request with `builtin_tools`. Available built-in tool flags include:

- `DateTime` — current date and time through `get_date_time`, in the gateway time zone (`parameters.timeZone`, default `America/Sao_Paulo`).
- `WebSearch`
- `AdvancedWebUsage` (disabled; returns an unavailable response. See [Changelogs](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/legal/changelogs.md).)
- `OpenUrl`
- `Code`
- `Request`
- `Remember`
- `GenerateWebPage`
- `GenerateDocument`
- `XPostsSearch`
- `ImageGeneration`

See [Built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md).

## MCP and protocol functions

Tools listed by an MCP source become available to the model with their declared schemas. MCP tool results can include text, images, and audio; media results are attached to the conversation as additional messages when supported.

Protocol functions expose HTTP callbacks or AIVAX callback URLs as model-callable tools. Remote protocol function sources are fetched and cached before their tools become available to the model.

See [Protocol functions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/protocol-functions.md) and [MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/mcp.md).

## Function interpreter

The function interpreter is deprecated. See [Function interpreter](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/function-interpreter.md).

## Workers

Workers call your external endpoint during gateway events, so your own code can allow, stop, or change the request. Configure worker events and endpoint details in the gateway parameters, and implement the event behavior at your endpoint. See [AI Workers](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/input-and-multimodality.html

# Input and multimodality

Send the conversation in `messages`, using the OpenAI roles `system`, `user`, `assistant`, and `tool`. With an AI Gateway, the gateway's system instructions are added to the `system` messages you send.

## Content parts

AIVAX accepts OpenAI-compatible message content parts for text, images, audio, videos, and files. The selected model must support the modality unless you ask AIVAX to [pre-process the media into text](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md).

```json
{
    "model": "@google/gemini-3-flash",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "text",
                    "text": "Describe these inputs briefly."
                },
                {
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {
                        "url": "data:image/png;base64,<BASE64_PNG_CONTENT>",
                        "detail": "auto"
                    }
                },
                {
                    "type": "input_audio",
                    "input_audio": {
                        "data": "<BASE64_WAV_CONTENT>",
                        "format": "wav"
                    }
                },
                {
                    "type": "file",
                    "file": {
                        "filename": "document.pdf",
                        "file_data": "data:application/pdf;base64,<BASE64_PDF_CONTENT>"
                    }
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

Supported content part mappings:

- `text`: Plain text.
- `image_url`: Image content. `image_url.url` can be an external URL or a base64 data URL. `image_url.detail` can be `low`, `high`, or `auto` when the model supports it.
- `video_url`: Video content. `video_url.url` can be an external URL or a base64 data URL. Prefer URLs for large videos.
- `input_audio`: Audio content. `input_audio.data` is base64 audio data, and `input_audio.format` names the format.
- `file`: File content. `file.filename` names the file, and `file.file_data` can be an external URL or a base64 data URL.

For video input, send a `video_url` content part. The following example uses a base64 data URL; for large videos, prefer a publicly reachable URL:

```json
{
    "model": "@google/gemini-3-flash",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "text",
                    "text": "Summarize the main actions in this video and identify any visible safety risks."
                },
                {
                    "type": "video_url",
                    "video_url": {
                        "url": "data:video/mp4;base64,<BASE64_MP4_CONTENT>"
                    }
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

External links must be accessible to AIVAX without authentication, firewall restrictions, or JavaScript-only rendering. The inference can fail because of failed downloads, redirects, blocked URLs, unsupported formats, or provider-specific size limits.

## Prompt shortcut

For a simple text-only request, you can send `prompt` instead of `messages`:

```json
{
    "model": "@google/gemini-3-flash",
    "prompt": "Say hello"
}
```

## Media requirements

Requests with media require a minimum account balance: files and videos need a higher balance than images and audio. Media is billed by the selected model according to its input rates. Review [Pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md) and [Plans and limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/limits.md) before using media in production.

When the selected model does not support a modality, convert the media into text with [multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md).

## When a multimodal request fails

Narrow down the problem:

1. Test a simple text message with the same model.
2. Test one small attachment.
3. Test the same attachment with `multimodal_resolver`.
4. Review the URL, format, size, and model modality support.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/caching.html

# Caching

Several caches affect an inference request. Prompt caching lowers the cost of input the provider has already processed. Other caches let AIVAX reuse media descriptions and remote definitions instead of fetching or processing them again.

## Prompt caching

Providers that support prompt caching reuse the processing of an identical request prefix. Cached input tokens are billed at the model's cache rate, which is lower than its input rate. Rates per model are listed on the dashboard **Models** page and in `GET /v1/models`.

The response reports cached input separately:

```json
{
    "usage": {
        "prompt_tokens": 412,
        "completion_tokens": 96,
        "total_tokens": 4604,
        "prompt_tokens_details": {
            "cached_tokens": 4096
        }
    }
}
```

`prompt_tokens` counts only the uncached input. Add `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` to it to get the full input size.

Send `prompt_cache_key` to group requests that share a prefix, such as the requests of one gateway or one user; AIVAX forwards it to the provider. Providers that do not support it ignore it.

### Keep the prefix stable

The cache matches only an identical prefix, so put stable content first and variable content last:

- Keep system instructions, tool definitions, and skill lists unchanged between requests. Gateway instructions are a stable prefix by default; remote instruction sources change it whenever their content changes.
- Do not put timestamps, request IDs, or user-specific values in the system instructions. Send them in the latest user message or in `metadata`.
- Append new messages to the end of the history instead of rewriting earlier ones. [Context truncation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md#context-window-and-truncation) and [tool message truncation](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md#tool-message-truncation) rewrite earlier messages and reduce cache hits.
- Retrieved RAG documents are inserted into the latest user message, so they do not break the prefix of earlier messages.

To check the hit rate on your own usage, see [why a prompt cache hit rate is low](https://aivax.net/blog/low-prompt-cache-hit-rate-prefix-breakers-compaction/).

## Multimodal pre-processing results

[Multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md) results are cached by content and engine. When the same media is resolved again with the same engine, AIVAX reuses the description and does not bill it again. Changing the engine processes and bills the content again.

This matters when you resend the full history: an image attached in the first turn is not described again on every later turn.

## Remote definitions

AIVAX caches resources that a gateway fetches from your servers:

| Resource | Default cache | Configurable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Remote instruction sources](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md#instructions) | 600 seconds | 0 to 86,400 seconds per source |
| [MCP](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/mcp.md) tool lists, server instructions, and remote skills | 600 seconds | `cacheDuration`, 0 to 86,400 seconds |
| [Protocol function sources](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/protocol-functions.md) | 10 minutes | No |

A failed fetch of a remote instruction source is cached for at most 30 seconds, so a temporary outage clears quickly. Tool calls are never cached: every MCP tool or protocol function call reaches your server.

Lower the cache duration while you develop a source, and raise it in production to reduce requests to your server and the latency of the first call.

## Server-side tool state

The server-side tool calls and results of recent turns are kept for one hour after their last use, so a request with the same `conversation_token` can restore them. This is a conversation state, not a response cache: AIVAX never returns a stored answer for a repeated request. See [Session reuse](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/session-reuse.md).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/tools.html

# Tools

Tools let the model request actions and data. AIVAX supports two execution models, and one request can use both:

| | Client-side tools | Server-side tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defined by | `tools` in the request or in the gateway | Gateway MCP sources, protocol functions, skills, shell, and built-in tools; `builtin_tools` in the request |
| Executed by | Your application | AIVAX |
| Returned to you | As `tool_calls`, which end the response | As `servertool` events while streaming; the final answer includes their effect |
| Results | Your application sends them back as `tool` messages | AIVAX adds them to the conversation and continues |

Use client-side tools when the action must run in your application, for example because it needs the user's local state or a credential that must not leave your system. Use server-side tools when AIVAX can perform the action, so a single request completes the whole task. See [MCP and protocol functions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/mcp-and-protocol-functions.md) and [Built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/built-in-tools.md).

## Client-side tools

Define client-side tools with the OpenAI `tools` format:

```json
{
    "model": "@openai/gpt-5-mini",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "What's the weather in Lisbon?"
        }
    ],
    "tools": [
        {
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": "get_weather",
                "description": "Returns the current weather for a city.",
                "parameters": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "city": { "type": "string" }
                    },
                    "required": ["city"]
                }
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

When the model calls a client-side tool, the response ends with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, and the calls are returned in `choices[].message.tool_calls`, or as `delta.tool_calls` when streaming. Run each call, then send the assistant message with its `tool_calls` and one `tool` message per call, using the same `tool_call_id`:

```json
{
    "model": "@openai/gpt-5-mini",
    "conversation_token": "weather-thread-7",
    "messages": [
        { "role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Lisbon?" },
        {
            "role": "assistant",
            "content": null,
            "tool_calls": [
                {
                    "id": "call_abc123",
                    "type": "function",
                    "function": { "name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\":\"Lisbon\"}" }
                }
            ]
        },
        {
            "role": "tool",
            "tool_call_id": "call_abc123",
            "content": "{\"temperature\":21,\"condition\":\"sunny\"}"
        }
    ],
    "tools": [ "..." ]
}
```

Send the same `tools` definitions again in the follow-up request. `tool_choice` and `parallel_tool_calls` are forwarded to the provider when the model supports them.

Tools defined in the gateway's raw `tools` parameter behave the same way: they are sent to the model, and your client runs them.

## Mixing client-side and server-side tools

In one request, AIVAX runs the server-side tools the model calls and continues generating. When the model calls a client-side tool, the response ends and returns those calls to you; any server-side tools requested in the same step have already run. After you send the client tool results, send the same `conversation_token` so the model still sees the server-side results of earlier steps; see [Session reuse](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/session-reuse.md).

## Requirements

- The model must support function calling. For a model without reliable native tool calling, a gateway can use a [tool handler](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md#tool-handler).
- Tool names must be unique across all tools of the request. The names `shell` and `read_skill` are reserved when the gateway uses the shell.
- Public API keys can send `tools`, but the gateway's server-side tools are not used; see [Limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/limits.md#public-api-keys).

Every tool adds its name, description, and schema to the input of each request. Expose only the tools the task needs, and give them specific names and restrictive schemas; see [Choosing the function name](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/mcp.md#choosing-the-function-name).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/mcp-and-protocol-functions.html

# MCP and protocol functions in inference

MCP tools and protocol functions are server-side tools that call your systems. AIVAX lists or loads their definitions, offers them to the model, and calls your server when the model selects one. Your client application does not run them and does not see their calls as messages.

| | [MCP sources](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/mcp.md) | [Protocol functions](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/protocol-functions.md) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What you run | An MCP server with Streamable HTTP | An HTTP endpoint per function, or a source URL that lists functions |
| Tool definitions | Discovered from the server's tool list | Declared in the gateway, or returned by a function source |
| Results | Text, images, and audio | Text |
| Best for | Catalogs of tools, systems that already speak MCP, tools shared by several agents | One or a few specific actions |

## Where to configure them

MCP sources and protocol functions are configured on an [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md#tools). The `chat/completions` request has no field to add them, so call the gateway by its ID or slug to use them.

A [worker](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md) can add an MCP source or a tool for a single request during the `message.received` event. Use it when the available tools depend on the user, such as tools scoped to the user's account.

## What happens during the request

1. Before the model runs, AIVAX loads the tool definitions. MCP tool lists and function sources are cached; see [Caching](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/caching.md#remote-definitions).
2. When the model calls one of these tools, AIVAX calls your server with the arguments.
3. The result is added to the conversation, and the model continues.
4. With streaming, each call produces `servertool` events with the states `Created`, then `Completed` or `Failed`; see [Streaming](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/streaming.md#server-side-tool-events).

The tool calls and results are not returned as messages. Send the same `conversation_token` on the next turn so the model keeps their results; see [Server-side context](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/server-side-context.md).

Return clear error text from your tool when an action cannot be completed, so the model can explain the failure or try another path. A [worker](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/workers.md) can replace the result of a tool call through the `tool.called` event.

## Public keys

Requests authenticated with a public API key do not use the gateway's MCP sources or protocol functions. Call a gateway with these tools from your server with a private key, or through a [chat client](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-clients.md).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/structured-output.html

# Structured output

Use structured responses when your application needs JSON output that matches a schema. AIVAX supports them through `response_schema`, `response_format`, and `json_only`.

```json
{
    "model": "@google/gemini-3.8-flash",
    "prompt": "Search for recent news about electric vehicles.",
    "stream": true,
    "builtin_tools": {
        "tools": [
            "WebSearch"
        ],
        "options": {
            "web_search_mode": "full"
        }
    },
    "response_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "news": {
                "type": "array",
                "items": {
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "title": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "description": "News title"
                        },
                        "summary": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "description": "News summary"
                        }
                    },
                    "required": ["title", "summary"]
                }
            }
        },
        "required": ["news"]
    }
}
```

`response_schema` enables JSON Healing. AIVAX asks the model for JSON, extracts JSON from the generated text or markdown blocks, validates it against the schema, and retries with validation feedback until the output is valid or the attempt limit is reached.


If your application cannot parse or validate the result, follow the [invalid JSON troubleshooting guide](https://aivax.net/blog/structured-output-healing-boundary/) before increasing the retry budget.

## Choose a field

| Field | Validation | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response_schema` | AIVAX validates the output and retries with feedback ([JSON Healing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/structured-responses/json-healing.md)). | Any model, including models without native structured output, and responses that use tools before the JSON. |
| `response_format` with `json_schema` | The provider enforces the schema natively; AIVAX also heals when `healing_options` is set or automatic JSON Healing is enabled on the account. | The model supports native structured output and you want the provider to constrain generation. |
| `json_only` | Returns only the final JSON, without the chat completion envelope. | The consumer is a program that expects a bare JSON body; see [JSON-only](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/structured-responses/json-only.md). |

With tools or reasoning, the model can call tools and reason first; the JSON is extracted from the final answer only. See [Reasoning and tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/structured-responses/reasoning-and-tools.md).

Structured output fields are not available with public API keys. When the attempt limit is reached, the request fails with `503 Service Unavailable`; see [JSON Healing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/structured-responses/json-healing.md#when-healing-fails).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/built-in-tools.html

# On-demand built-in tools

Use `builtin_tools` to enable AIVAX [built-in tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md) for a direct request without creating a gateway:

```json
{
    "model": "@google/gemini-3.8-flash",
    "prompt": "Search for recent news about electric vehicles.",
    "stream": true,
    "builtin_tools": {
        "tools": [
            "WebSearch"
        ],
        "options": {
            "web_search_mode": "full",
            "web_search_max_results": 5
        }
    }
}
```

Built-in tools include `DateTime`, `WebSearch`, `AdvancedWebUsage` (disabled; returns an unavailable response; see [Changelogs](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/legal/changelogs.md)), `OpenUrl`, `Code`, `Request`, `Remember`, `GenerateWebPage`, `GenerateDocument`, `XPostsSearch`, and `ImageGeneration`.

`DateTime` exposes `get_date_time`, a no-argument tool returning the current date, time, English weekday, time zone, UTC offset, and ISO 8601 timestamp. It uses the gateway time zone (default `America/Sao_Paulo`); send `time_zone` with an IANA identifier to override it for one request. This setting is independent of the user's browser time zone. See [Current Date and Time](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md#current-date-and-time) for configuration and output examples.

On-demand tools are suitable for occasional calls, prototypes, and integrations that do not need a persistent gateway. If the same application always uses the same tools, prefer configuring them in an AI Gateway so the policy is centralized.

## Combine with a gateway

When `model` is a gateway, `builtin_tools` adds tools to the ones the gateway already enables; it does not remove gateway tools. `options` applies to the tools of this request. Public API keys cannot send `builtin_tools`.

Built-in tools are server-side tools: their calls appear as `servertool` events while streaming and are not returned as messages. Reuse the `conversation_token` so later turns keep their results; see [Server-side context](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/server-side-context.md). Each tool is billed according to its own rates; see [Built-in tools pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md#pricing-and-limits).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/streaming.html

# Streaming

Set `stream: true` to receive the response as server-sent events (SSE) while it is generated. Each event is a `data:` line with a JSON `chat.completion.chunk`, and the stream ends with `data: [DONE]`. OpenAI-compatible SDKs parse this format directly.

Use streaming for user-facing chats, so the user sees progress while reasoning and tools run. Streaming also keeps data flowing, so long requests rarely hit proxy timeouts.

## Event types

| Chunk contains | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `choices[].delta.content` | A fragment of the answer text. |
| `choices[].delta.reasoning` | A fragment of the model's reasoning, when the model returns it. |
| `choices[].delta.tool_calls` | A [client-side tool](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/tools.md) call. The stream then ends with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. |
| `servertool` | A [server-side tool](#server-side-tool-events) state change. `choices` is empty. |
| `usage` | The last chunk before `[DONE]`, with `finish_reason` and token usage. |
| `error` | A failure after the stream started; see [Errors during a stream](#errors-during-a-stream). |

Every chunk includes `id`, the AIVAX message ID (`aivx_...`), `model`, and `provider`. The last chunk before `[DONE]` also includes `conversation_token`. Store both to continue the conversation; see [Session reuse](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/session-reuse.md).

Preserve the order in which events arrive. Reasoning, tool events, and answer text of one assistant turn can be interleaved.

## Server-side tool events

While AIVAX runs a built-in tool, MCP tool, or protocol function, it sends chunks with a `servertool` object:

```json
{
    "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
    "choices": [],
    "servertool": {
        "name": "web_search",
        "id": "call-example-id-0",
        "contents": "{\"query\":\"weather forecast today\"}",
        "state": "Created",
        "explanation": null
    }
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Tool name. |
| `id` | Tool call ID. All events of one call share it. |
| `contents` | Tool arguments as a JSON string. |
| `state` | `Created` when the call starts, then `Completed` or `Failed`. |
| `explanation` | `{ "reason", "goal" }` when [tool explanations](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/response-rendering/tool-explanations.md) are enabled and the model supplied them; otherwise `null`. |

To receive reasoning and tool activity as text blocks inside `delta.content` instead of separate fields, use `rendering_mode: "textual_blocks"`; see [Chat presentation guidance](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/response-rendering/chat-presentation-guidance.md).

## Usage chunk

The last chunk before `[DONE]` has an empty `delta`, the final `finish_reason`, and `usage`:

```json
{
    "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
    "choices": [
        { "index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop", "delta": {} }
    ],
    "usage": {
        "prompt_tokens": 412,
        "completion_tokens": 96,
        "total_tokens": 4604,
        "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 4096, "audio_tokens": 0 }
    },
    "conversation_token": "support-ticket-1042"
}
```

`prompt_tokens` excludes cached input; see [Caching](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/caching.md).

## Keep-alive

While a stream is open, AIVAX sends a keep-alive event with the data `%ping%` every 15 seconds, so proxies do not close an idle connection during long tool calls. Ignore events whose data is `%ping%`. If your SSE parser expects JSON in every event, skip these events or disable the keep-alive.

To disable the keep-alive, send the request header:

```text
Sse-Stream-Options: no-ping
```

Disable it only when nothing between your client and AIVAX closes idle connections.

## Errors during a stream

Once the stream starts, the HTTP status is already `200`. A failure is sent as a chunk with `finish_reason: "error"` and an `error` object, followed by `[DONE]`:

```json
{
    "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
    "choices": [
        { "index": 0, "finish_reason": "error", "delta": { "content": "" } }
    ],
    "error": {
        "code": "service_unavailable",
        "message": "The inference provider is unavailable right now. Please, try again later."
    }
}
```

Check every chunk for `error` and treat it as a failed request. Text already received belongs to an incomplete answer; discard it or mark it as incomplete. For integrated models, provider error details are not returned; for gateways that use your own provider key, the provider's message is returned as is.

When a provider fails before any data was sent, AIVAX retries the request on another eligible provider, so the client sees no error.

## Streaming with `json_only`

With `json_only: true`, AIVAX generates the complete JSON first and sends it as a single SSE event containing the raw JSON, followed by `[DONE]`. The event is not a `chat.completion.chunk`. See [JSON-only](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/structured-responses/json-only.md).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/custom-json.html

# Custom provider request body

Use `extra_body` to send provider-specific options. When a gateway uses your own provider API key and an OpenAI-compatible provider endpoint, `extra_body` merges custom JSON into the provider request body:

```json
{
    "model": "my-custom-model:abc4",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Explain the tradeoff."
        }
    ],
    "extra_body": {
        "reasoning": {
            "enabled": true
        }
    }
}
```

`extra_body` is not allowed with integrated AIVAX models.

Reasoning parameters differ by provider and model. See [how to set reasoning effort across providers](https://aivax.net/blog/reasoning-is-a-protocol-not-just-a-model-setting/) before choosing provider-specific options.

Use `extra_body` for options that AIVAX does not expose as a request field, such as a provider's reasoning switch. Prefer the standard fields, such as `reasoning_effort`, when they exist, because they also work after you change the provider. The JSON is merged at the root of the provider request and can overwrite fields AIVAX sets, so send only the keys the provider documents.

Send `extra_body` as a field of the JSON request body. When using the OpenAI Python SDK, nest it inside the SDK's `extra_body` argument, as in `extra_body={"extra_body": {...}}`, because the SDK's own `extra_body` only adds fields to the request; see [Using via SDKs](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/using-sdks.md#send-aivax-fields).

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.html

# Multimodal pre-processing

Use `multimodal_resolver` when the main model should receive a textual description of media instead of the original media object. This is useful for text-first models or when you want AIVAX to normalize files before the main inference. The object chooses an engine for each content type; omitted or `null` types are sent to the main model unchanged.

```json
{
    "model": "@meta/llama-3.3-70b",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "text",
                    "text": "Describe this file briefly."
                },
                {
                    "type": "file",
                    "file": {
                        "filename": "document.pdf",
                        "file_data": "data:application/pdf;base64,<BASE64_PDF_CONTENT>"
                    }
                }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "multimodal_resolver": {
        "imageEngine": "InferenceLow",
        "audioEngine": "Stt",
        "fileEngine": "InferenceHigh"
    }
}
```

| Field | Accepted engines |
| --- | --- |
| `imageEngine` | `InferenceLow`, `InferenceHigh`, `Ocr` |
| `audioEngine` | `InferenceLow`, `InferenceHigh`, `Stt` |
| `videoEngine` | `InferenceLow`, `InferenceHigh` |
| `fileEngine` | `InferenceLow`, `InferenceHigh`, `Ocr` |

`Inference` is accepted as an alias of `InferenceLow`. The engines work as follows:

- `InferenceLow` describes the content with a smaller, lower-cost multimodal model.
- `InferenceHigh` describes the content with a larger multimodal model that is more accurate and costs more.
- `Ocr` extracts the text of images and files with the same extraction service as [Fetch and OCR](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/web-foundation/fetch-and-ocr.md), billed in Processing Units. It accepts base64 data URIs and public URLs.
- `Stt` transcribes the speech in the audio with the default [speech-to-text](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/pricing.md) model and is billed per second of audio. Music and ambient sounds are not described.

With `InferenceLow` or `InferenceHigh`, `fileEngine` sends PDFs to the multimodal model and converts other file types with OCR. With `Ocr`, every file, including PDFs, is converted with OCR.

Results are cached by content and engine for reuse, so the same media resolved with the same engine is not billed again. Changing the engine processes and bills the content again. See [Caching](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/caching.md).

## Choose an engine

| Content | Engine | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scanned documents, screenshots of text, forms | `Ocr` | The text matters more than the layout or the visual content. |
| Photos, charts, diagrams | `InferenceLow` or `InferenceHigh` | The model must understand what the image shows. Use `InferenceHigh` when small details matter. |
| Calls, voice notes, meetings | `Stt` | The words spoken are what matters. |
| Audio where tone, music, or sounds matter | `InferenceLow` or `InferenceHigh` | A transcription would lose the information. |
| Video | `InferenceLow` or `InferenceHigh` | Only multimodal descriptions are available. |

The main model receives only the resulting text, so it cannot answer questions about details the description left out. If users ask follow-up questions about the same media, a model that accepts the media directly usually gives better answers. To set the engines for every request, configure them on an [AI Gateway](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/ai-gateways/concepts.md#multimodal-pre-processing) as `multimodalResolverParameters`.

## Deprecated `multimodal_preprocess`

The `multimodal_preprocess` flags remain accepted for compatibility but are deprecated. Use `multimodal_resolver` instead; when both are sent, `multimodal_resolver` is used. The flags map to the new engines as follows:

| Legacy flag | Equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `Image` | `imageEngine: "InferenceLow"` |
| `Audio` | `audioEngine: "InferenceLow"` |
| `Video` | `videoEngine: "InferenceLow"` |
| `File` | `fileEngine: "InferenceLow"` |
| `OtherFiles` | `fileEngine: "Ocr"` |
| `All` | All of the above, with `fileEngine: "InferenceLow"` |

Because one engine now covers every file type, `OtherFiles` alone also converts PDFs with OCR, and `File` alone also converts non-PDF files with OCR. Previously, the file types outside the selected flag were sent to the main model unchanged.

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/context-truncation.html

# Context truncation

Context truncation keeps long conversations within a maximum input size. An AI Gateway can limit the input with `contextMaximumSize`, choose what happens when a conversation exceeds it with `contextOverflowAction`, and shorten old tool results with `toolContextCount`. Configure them in **Context window management** in the gateway editor or in the gateway parameters.

These are gateway settings; requests cannot override them. Your application still sends the full history it stores, and truncation only changes what the model receives for that request.

## Maximum context size

`contextMaximumSize` is the maximum approximate number of input tokens sent to the model. When it is not set, AIVAX does not limit the input, and the request fails only if it exceeds the model's own context window.

The size is an estimate, not the provider's token count. It includes:

- Conversation messages, including documents inserted by [RAG](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md#rag).
- System instructions.
- Tool definitions, including server-side tools.
- The response schema, when one is requested.

Because the estimate can differ from the provider's tokenizer, set `contextMaximumSize` below the model's real context window to leave a margin, especially for media-heavy conversations.

On the Free plan, the input context is capped, even when the model or the gateway allows more. See [Limits](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/limits.md#context-window) for the value.

## Overflow actions

When the estimated input exceeds the limit, the gateway follows `contextOverflowAction`:

| Action | Behavior | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Throw` (default) | Returns an error instead of calling the model. | Every message matters, such as a document review, so the application decides what to remove. |
| `Truncate` | Removes the oldest conversation messages until they fit, then continues, even if the full prompt still exceeds the limit. | Long-lived chats in which old turns lose relevance, such as support conversations. |
| `TruncateHard` | Truncates like `Truncate`, then returns an error if the full prompt still exceeds the limit. | You want truncation, but never a request larger than the limit. |

The gateway editor offers `Throw` and `Truncate`; set `TruncateHard` through the API.

### How truncation removes messages

`Truncate` and `TruncateHard` remove messages from the beginning of the conversation, one at a time:

- System messages are never removed.
- The last remaining user message is never removed, so the model always receives the current request.
- Tool results whose tool call was removed are also removed, so the conversation stays valid for the provider.
- Messages are removed until the conversation messages fit the limit. System instructions, retrieved RAG documents, and tool definitions are not counted in this step, so with `Truncate` the full prompt can still exceed the limit. `TruncateHard` measures the full prompt again and fails if it does not fit.

Truncation does not summarize removed messages. When the model needs facts from early turns, keep them in the system instructions, in a [collection](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/rag/collections.md), or in [memories](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/tools/builtin-tools.md).

### When the check runs

The check runs before every model generation of a request, not only once. In an agentic request, a large tool result can make the conversation exceed the limit after some tools already ran. With `Throw`, the request then fails at that point; with `Truncate`, older messages are removed and the loop continues. See [Processing pipeline](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/processing-pipeline.md) for where the check runs relative to the other steps.

The check uses the conversation before [multimodal pre-processing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/multimodal-pre-processing.md), so media counts by its estimated original size, not by the size of its textual description.

## Tool message truncation

`toolContextCount` controls how many recent tool response messages keep their original content. When it is set to a value greater than zero, older tool messages remain in the conversation but their content is replaced with:

```text
[tool response truncated - call this tool again]
```

This applies to every tool result sent to the model, including results of [client-side tools](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/tools.md) and server-side tools. It reduces context usage in long agentic conversations whose tools return large payloads that are only relevant once, such as search results. Avoid it when an early tool result remains important later, and use it only when the model can safely call the tool again.

Rewriting older tool messages also changes the request prefix, which can lower the [prompt cache](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/caching.md) hit rate; to check this on your own usage, see [why a prompt cache hit rate is low](https://aivax.net/blog/low-prompt-cache-hit-rate-prefix-breakers-compaction/).

## Example

The following gateway fragment keeps support conversations under 32,000 estimated tokens and keeps only the last three tool results:

```json
{
  "contextMaximumSize": 32000,
  "contextOverflowAction": "Truncate",
  "toolContextCount": 3
}
```

---

Source: https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/moderation.html

# Moderation

Moderation enforces safety policy on user requests before the main model answers them. Use it to block unsafe or out-of-policy requests in user-facing assistants. Configure it in the **Content Moderation** section of the gateway editor or in `parameters.moderationParameters`.

Moderation is an AI Gateway setting; direct `chat/completions` calls with a model name do not run it, and requests cannot change it.

## Choose a mode

The `moderationParameters.mode` field selects how moderation runs:

| | `LayeredGuardrail` (default) | `SelfAssessment` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who decides | An independent safeguard model, before the main model | The main model itself |
| Extra inference | Yes, billed as moderation usage | No |
| Added latency | One safeguard inference | None |
| Isolation | Independent from the main model and its instructions | Depends on the main model's judgment |
| Model requirements | None | The main model must support tool calling |

- `LayeredGuardrail`: An independent safeguard model analyzes the conversation's input text before the main model. Flagged conversations are blocked, and the main model responds with a refusal. Moderation usage is billed as described in [Inference pricing](https://docs.aivax.net/docs/inference/chat-completions/concepts.md#pricing).
- `SelfAssessment`: No separate safeguard model runs, so there is no moderation analysis charge. The main model receives moderation instructions built from the same category sensitivity levels and additional rules, plus an internal refusal tool. When the model judges that the latest request reaches the boundary of an enabled category, it calls the tool with a reason, the violated categories, and a final message for the user. The inference ends immediately, other tool calls from that turn are skipped, the final message is returned as the assistant reply, and the response is marked as a refusal.

Because `SelfAssessment` relies on the main model's judgment instead of an independent classifier, it trades lower latency and cost for weaker isolation: it is not an independent layer, and enforcement quality depends on the model. Prefer `LayeredGuardrail` when jailbreak attempts are a real risk.

## Categories

In `LayeredGuardrail` mode, when at least one moderation category is enabled, AIVAX sends the available textual conversation to a safeguard model. The safeguard evaluates the latest user request in the context established by the conversation and returns a score from 0 to 10 for every category.

| Category | Gateway property | What the safeguard evaluates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Violence and hate speech** | `violenceThreshold` | Violence, hate, extremism, threats, or encouragement of physical harm. |
| **Sexual and explicit content** | `sexualExplicitThreshold` | Sexually explicit or adult content. |
| **Political topics** | `politicalThreshold` | Political persuasion, campaigning, manipulation, or highly political content. |
| **Dangerous content** | `dangerousContentThreshold` | Weapons, explosives, cyber abuse, self-harm, or other dangerous acts and instructions. |
| **Jailbreak attempts** | `jailbreakThreshold` | Attempts to override instructions, reveal protected instructions, exfiltrate data, or inject prompts. |

## Understand sensitivity levels

The value configured in the gateway is a **sensitivity level** from `0` to `10`, not the safeguard score itself. A higher level lowers the score required to block the input. Values outside this range are rejected when the gateway is saved.

| Sensitivity level | Safeguard scores that block |
| ---: | --- |
| `0` | Category disabled |
| `1` | `10` |
| `3` | `8`–`10` |
| `5` | `6`–`10` |
| `8` | `3`–`10` |
| `10` | `1`–`10` |

For enabled categories, the blocking cutoff is `11 - sensitivity level`. A safeguard score of `0` never blocks. Configure each category independently; the request is blocked when any enabled category reaches its cutoff.

In `SelfAssessment` mode, the same sensitivity levels define the boundary the main model must enforce, although there is no numeric safeguard score.

## Add gateway-specific rules

**Additional moderation rules** let a gateway administrator describe policy that is not fully expressed by the built-in category descriptions. The safeguard reads these rules together with the built-in policy and uses them to calibrate all five scores. In `SelfAssessment` mode, the main model receives the same rules with its moderation instructions.

For example:

```text
Allow users to describe accidents and injuries when asking for insurance coverage or assistance.
Treat requests for instructions to cause an accident or harm someone as dangerous content.
```

Additional rules guide classification; they do not create a separate score or block an input directly. At least one category must have a sensitivity level above `0` for moderation to run. In the example above, enable **Dangerous content** so the safeguard score can produce a blocking decision.

Write rules as short policy statements with explicit allowed and disallowed cases. Do not include secrets, credentials, or private operational data because the rules are stored with the gateway configuration and sent to the safeguard model during moderation.

The following gateway fragment enables different sensitivity levels and gives the safeguard domain-specific guidance. The values are an example, not a recommended production baseline:

```json
{
  "moderationParameters": {
    "mode": "LayeredGuardrail",
    "violenceThreshold": 4,
    "sexualExplicitThreshold": 4,
    "politicalThreshold": 2,
    "dangerousContentThreshold": 6,
    "jailbreakThreshold": 7,
    "additionalRules": "Allow descriptions of accidents and injuries for insurance support. Treat instructions to cause accidents or harm someone as dangerous content."
  }
}
```

## What happens when an input is blocked

When any enabled category reaches its cutoff:

1. AIVAX marks the original conversation messages as unavailable to the main inference request.
